items.sentence: Look! The chef ___ a new dish right now — you can smell it.

explain.why: “Look!” dan “right now — you can smell it” nunjuk kejadian yang lagi jalan. Jadi “is preparing” yang pas.
explain.rule: Kejadian yang lagi jalan pakai am, is, atau are + kata kerja -ing. Kebiasaan yang berulang pakai bentuk sekarang biasa.
explain.memory: Ada “Look!”, berarti lihat bentuk -ing-nya.

distractors.misconception: habitual-aspect overgeneralization
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang rutinitas, padahal masakannya lagi dibikin saat itu.

distractors.misconception: confusing in-progress with completed result
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang masakannya udah jadi, padahal masih dibikin.

distractors.misconception: missing subject-verb agreement / bare form
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar nggak cocok sama subjek orang ketiga tunggal.

items.sentence: She ___ to Lisbon exactly once, in 2019, before the pandemic changed everything.

explain.why: “in 2019” itu rentang yang udah tutup, jadi past simple yang dipakai, bukan present perfect.
explain.rule: Present perfect nggak bisa jalan bareng keterangan waktu lampau yang pasti. Contohnya “yesterday”, “in 2019”, atau “last week”.
explain.memory: Ada tanggal pasti, berarti past simple.

distractors.misconception: present-perfect-for-any-past-event
distractors.whyFailsId: tahun “2019” maku kejadiannya di titik lampau yang udah kelar.

distractors.misconception: aspect confusion (progressive for a single completed trip)
distractors.whyFailsId: past continuous bikin latar yang lagi jalan, padahal perjalanannya udah kelar.

distractors.misconception: tense-timeline mismatch
distractors.whyFailsId: present simple nggak bisa nyebut kejadian lampau yang tanggalnya jelas.

items.sentence: Which completion shows a decision made only at the moment of speaking? A: 'The phone's ringing.' B: 'Don't worry, I ___ it.'

explain.why: “Will” dipakai buat keputusan yang baru diambil pas ngomong, misalnya nawarin bantuan.
explain.rule: Pakai “will” buat keputusan mendadak dan tawaran bantuan. Pakai present continuous atau “going to” buat rencana yang udah disusun lebih dulu.
explain.memory: Keputusan yang seketika, pakai “will” seketika.

distractors.misconception: treats spontaneous offers as pre-arranged plans
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang rencananya udah diatur atau udah jalan, bukan keputusan pas ngomong.

distractors.misconception: present simple used for a one-off future act
distractors.whyFailsId: present simple buat kebiasaan dan jadwal, bukan tawaran mendadak.

distractors.misconception: structural error: double -ing after 'going to'
distractors.whyFailsId: setelah “going to” wajib nyusul kata kerja bentuk dasar.

items.sentence: Visitors ___ leave their bags at the front desk; it's a museum rule, not a choice.

explain.why: Kalimatnya bilang sendiri ini aturan museum, bukan pilihan. Itu ciri kewajiban.
explain.rule: “Must” dan “have to” bilang wajib. “Can”, “may”, dan “could” bilang boleh atau mungkin.
explain.memory: Kalau ini aturan, pakai “must”.

distractors.misconception: obligation read as ability/permission
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang sesuatu diperbolehkan, bukan diwajibkan aturan.

distractors.misconception: obligation read as formal permission
distractors.whyFailsId: ngasih izin, nggak nuntut keharusan apa pun.

distractors.misconception: obligation read as a polite hypothetical
distractors.whyFailsId: memperhalus permintaan atau nyebut kemungkinan saja.

items.sentence: Which option expresses the strongest negative deduction supported by the evidence? The lights are off and the car isn't in the driveway, so they ___ be home.

explain.why: “Can’t” bilang kesimpulan negatif yang kamu yakin banget dari bukti yang ada.
explain.rule: Buat kesimpulan negatif yang kamu yakin, pakai “can’t”, bukan “mustn’t” yang artinya larangan.
explain.memory: Yakin nggak mungkin: pakai “can’t”, bukan “mustn’t”.

distractors.misconception: negative obligation confused with negative deduction
distractors.whyFailsId: artinya nggak boleh dilakuin, bukan kesimpulan kalau sesuatu mustahil.

distractors.misconception: underestimates the strength of the evidence
distractors.whyFailsId: buktinya kelewat kuat buat dugaan yang selemah ini.

distractors.misconception: deduction confused with expectation/advice
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang apa yang sebaiknya, bukan kesimpulan dari bukti.

items.sentence: Which completion states this as a general fact that is always true, not a prediction about one occasion? If you heat ice, it ___.

explain.why: Es dipanasin memang selalu mencair, bukan cuma sekali. Fakta kayak gini pakai present simple dua-duanya.
explain.rule: Zero conditional: if + present simple, terus present simple lagi. Rumus ini buat fakta yang selalu bener.
explain.memory: Selalu bener? Present ketemu present.

distractors.misconception: general truth treated as a one-time prediction
distractors.whyFailsId: bahasanya bener, tapi ini ramalan satu kejadian.

distractors.misconception: real condition treated as hypothetical
distractors.whyFailsId: “would” buat keadaan yang nggak nyata, padahal es memang mencair.

distractors.misconception: past tense used for a timeless fact
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk lampau bikin fakta itu kayak udah lewat.

items.sentence: If I ___ the lottery, I would travel the world — but let's be honest, it's not going to happen.

explain.why: Kalimatnya sendiri bilang menang lotre itu nggak akan kejadian. Keadaan kayak gini pakai past simple di anak kalimat if.
explain.rule: Second conditional: if + past simple, terus would + kata kerja dasar. Bentuk ini buat keadaan yang cuma dibayangin atau kecil banget kemungkinannya.
explain.memory: Nggak nyata sekarang: bentuknya lampau, maknanya bukan lampau.

distractors.misconception: if-clause verb form mismatched with 'would' in the main clause
distractors.whyFailsId: pola “if + present” itu nggak dipasangin sama “would” di hasilnya.

distractors.misconception: duplicating 'would' in both clauses
distractors.whyFailsId: “would” cuma berdiri di anak kalimat hasil, bukan di bagian if.

distractors.misconception: real/likely framing applied to an admittedly unlikely event
distractors.whyFailsId: pembicaranya sendiri bilang hal itu nggak akan kejadian.

items.sentence: Which completion most explicitly leaves the unknown builder out of the sentence? The bridge ___ in 1932; nobody today remembers who built it.

explain.why: Pasif tanpa bagian “by” lebih pas kalau pelakunya nggak diketahui atau nggak penting.
explain.rule: Kalimat pasif dibentuk dari be + bentuk ketiga kata kerja (past participle). Bagian “by + pelaku” dibuang kalau pelakunya nggak diketahui, udah jelas, atau nggak penting.
explain.memory: Kalau nggak tahu siapa pelakunya, buang “by”-nya.

distractors.misconception: active voice used despite an unknown/irrelevant agent
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimat aktif nuntut pelaku yang disebut, padahal pembangunnya nggak diketahui.

distractors.misconception: malformed passive/perfect blend
distractors.whyFailsId: susunan ini bukan bentuk kata kerja yang sah.

distractors.misconception: adds a vague, uninformative agent instead of omitting it
distractors.whyFailsId: bener tata bahasanya, tapi pelaku samar yang gini nggak nambah info.

items.sentence: Apply conventional backshift to report the earlier state: Yesterday she said, ‘I am tired.’ Today we report that she ___ tired.

explain.why: Kata pelapornya “said” dan keterangan “Yesterday” naruh laporannya di lampau, dan keadaannya udah lewat. Jadi “am” mundur jadi “was”.
explain.rule: Kalau laporannya netral atau isinya udah nggak berlaku, tense-nya mundur satu langkah. Present simple jadi past simple. Present continuous jadi past continuous. Present perfect jadi past perfect.
explain.memory: Laporan yang netral biasanya mundur satu langkah.

distractors.misconception: no backshift applied
distractors.whyFailsId: laporannya netral dan keadaannya udah lewat, jadi bentuk presentnya mundur.

distractors.misconception: backshift target confused with present perfect
distractors.whyFailsId: present simple mundurnya ke past simple, bukan ke present perfect.

distractors.misconception: tense category changed instead of shifted one step back
distractors.whyFailsId: ini malah maju ke masa depan, bukan mundur satu langkah.

items.sentence: On the way home, she stopped ___ some bread because the bakery was still open.

explain.why: “Stop to buy” berarti dia berhenti sebentar buat beli roti, jadi bentuk to-nya nyatain tujuan.
explain.rule: “Stop” + bentuk -ing berarti kamu berhenti dari kegiatan itu. “Stop” + to + kata kerja berarti berhenti sebentar buat ngerjain hal lain.
explain.memory: “Stop to do” berarti berhenti demi satu tujuan.

distractors.misconception: gerund used where a purpose-infinitive is needed
distractors.whyFailsId: “stop buying” berarti dia berhenti dari kebiasaan beli roti, bukan satu kali mampir.

distractors.misconception: bare infinitive used instead of the required to-infinitive
distractors.whyFailsId: makna tujuan di “stop” minta bentuk pakai to, bukan bentuk dasar.

distractors.misconception: perfect gerund used where a simple purpose clause is needed
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk ini bilang tindakannya udah kelar lebih dulu, bukan tujuan berhentinya.

items.sentence: Between these two routes, the coastal road is ___ than the mountain pass.

explain.why: Susunan “more scenic ... than” mbandingin tepat dua jalur. Itu memang tugas bentuk “lebih” (comparative).
explain.rule: Bentuk “lebih” (comparative) jalan bareng “than” buat mbandingin dua hal. Bentuk “paling” (superlative) pakai the plus -est atau most buat nunjuk juara satu kelompok.
explain.memory: Dua hal pakai -er atau more. Satu kelompok pakai -est atau most.

distractors.misconception: superlative used for a two-item comparison
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk “paling” nunjuk juara kelompok, di sini cuma dua jalur.

distractors.misconception: base adjective used without comparative marking
distractors.whyFailsId: kata sifatnya polos, “than” jadi nggak punya pijakan.

distractors.misconception: superlative used without 'the', still wrong scope
distractors.whyFailsId: “the” hilang, dan bentuk “paling” tetap salah cakupan.

items.sentence: You haven't finished the report yet, ___?

explain.why: “haven’t” di induk kalimatnya negatif dan kata bantunya “have”. Jadi ekornya positif dan tetep pakai “have”.
explain.rule: Ekor pertanyaan biasanya ngebalik positif-negatif induk kalimatnya dan ngulang kata bantu yang sama. Ekor yang positif-negatifnya sama kepakai buat nunjukin kesetujuan atau kaget, kayak “So you are coming, are you?”.
explain.memory: Kalimat negatif biasanya dapet ekor positif.

distractors.misconception: tag polarity copied instead of reversed
distractors.whyFailsId: di kalimat ini induknya udah negatif, jadi ekor negatif lagi nggak pas.

distractors.misconception: wrong auxiliary borrowed from a different tense
distractors.whyFailsId: induk kalimatnya pakai present perfect, jadi kata bantunya nggak nyambung.

distractors.misconception: wrong auxiliary substituted (present simple instead of present perfect)
distractors.whyFailsId: kata bantu di ekornya wajib sama kayak yang di pernyataannya.

items.sentence: I ___ dinner when the power suddenly went out.

explain.why: Masak udah jalan sebagai latar waktu listrik tiba-tiba padam.
explain.rule: Past continuous pakai was atau were + kata kerja -ing buat bangun latarnya. Past simple ngelaporin kejadian yang nyela.
explain.memory: Latar pakai -ing, penyela pakai past simple.

distractors.misconception: treats both clauses as sequential completed events
distractors.whyFailsId: kesannya masakannya udah selesai sebelum listrik padam.

distractors.misconception: confuses interrupted past action with present perfect result
distractors.whyFailsId: present perfect nggak bisa bareng waktu lampau yang pasti.

distractors.misconception: bare present form used for a past narrative
distractors.whyFailsId: “went out” naruh kalimatnya di masa lalu.

items.sentence: She ___ three novels this year, and she's already working on a fourth.

explain.why: “three novels” ngitung hasil yang udah kelar, dan “already working on a fourth” nunjukin novel keempatnya baru mulai. Jadi present perfect simple yang pas.
explain.rule: Pakai present perfect simple buat tindakan yang udah kelar dan hasilnya masih kerasa sekarang. Pakai present perfect continuous kalau yang ditonjolin lamanya atau berulangnya kegiatan.
explain.memory: Hasil kehitung pakai simple; proses yang masih jalan pakai continuous.

distractors.misconception: over-applies continuous aspect whenever a time span like 'this year' appears
distractors.whyFailsId: “has been writing” nyorot prosesnya jalan serentak, bukan tiga novel yang udah tuntas.

distractors.misconception: shifts to a fixed past narrative tense
distractors.whyFailsId: “was writing” ngunci kegiatannya di momen lampau yang tutup, padahal “this year” masih kebuka.

distractors.misconception: treats the sentence as a habitual routine
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimatnya nglaporin capaian yang kekumpul sejauh ini, bukan kebiasaan berulang.

items.sentence: By the time the ambulance arrived, the neighbors ___ first aid.

explain.why: “By the time” plus kejadian past simple bikin titik acuan. Kejadian yang kelar sebelum titik itu pakai past perfect.
explain.rule: Past perfect pakai had + bentuk ketiga kata kerja (past participle). Bentuk ini nandain kejadian yang lebih dulu di antara dua kejadian lampau.
explain.memory: Ada “by the time X happened”, kejadian satunya butuh “had” di depan.

distractors.misconception: uses past simple for the earlier event, flattening the sequence
distractors.whyFailsId: “by the time” jadi kehilangan maknanya “sebelum titik itu”.

distractors.misconception: confuses completed prior action with an action still in progress at the reference point
distractors.whyFailsId: pertolongannya udah kelar sebelum ambulans nyampe, bukan masih jalan.

distractors.misconception: bare present form in a past narrative
distractors.whyFailsId: seluruh kalimatnya udah dipatok ke masa lalu sama “arrived”.

items.sentence: Which completion shows the action already in progress at that exact moment? Don't call at 8pm — I ___ dinner with my in-laws then.

explain.why: Makan malamnya masih jalan tepat jam delapan, dan itu yang dinyatain future continuous.
explain.rule: Future continuous “will be” + kata kerja -ing nggambarin tindakan yang masih jalan di waktu tertentu nanti. Future perfect “will have” + past participle (bentuk ke-3 kata kerja) nggambarin tindakan yang udah kelar sebelum waktu itu.
explain.memory: Masih jalan nanti pakai “will be” + -ing; udah kelar pakai “will have” + bentuk ke-3.

distractors.misconception: uses a bare future form without marking the ongoing nature of the action
distractors.whyFailsId: “will have” bener tapi cuma nyebut rencananya, bukan makan malam yang udah jalan.

distractors.misconception: wrongly applies future perfect, implying the dinner is finished by 8pm
distractors.whyFailsId: konteksnya bilang makan malamnya jalan PADA jam delapan, jadi belum kelar.

distractors.misconception: drops the future marker entirely, defaulting to present simple
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimatnya nyebut waktu nanti yang jelas jadi minta bentuk masa depan.

items.sentence: The fire was spreading fast, but the firefighters ___ everyone out of the building.

explain.why: Ini satu keberhasilan tertentu di keadaan sulit, jadi yang pas “was/were able to”.
explain.rule: Pakai “could” buat kemampuan umum di masa lalu. Pakai “was/were able to” atau “managed to” buat satu keberhasilan tertentu.
explain.memory: Berhasil sekali di keadaan mendesak: “was able to”, bukan “could”.

distractors.misconception: extends general-ability 'could' to a single specific achievement
distractors.whyFailsId: “could” biasanya bilang kemampuan umum, bukan satu keberhasilan yang mendesak.

distractors.misconception: uses present-tense modal for a clearly past narrative
distractors.whyFailsId: “was spreading” udah maku kalimat ini di masa lalu.

distractors.misconception: drops the modal/auxiliary entirely
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimat ini butuh kata bantu buat nyatain kemampuan.

items.sentence: Which option expresses the strongest positive past deduction supported by the evidence? The lights are still off and his car isn't here — he ___ left for work already.

explain.why: Lampu mati dan mobilnya nggak ada itu bukti kuat, jadi pas sama “must have” + past participle.
explain.rule: “Must have” berarti yakin sesuatu kejadian; “can’t have” berarti yakin sesuatu nggak kejadian. Beda dari “should have” yang nyoal kewajiban terlewat, dan “might have” yang cuma kemungkinan.
explain.memory: Bukti kuat mendukung: “must have”. Bukti kuat nyangkal: “can’t have”.

distractors.misconception: confuses the polarity of the deduction
distractors.whyFailsId: bukti lampu mati dan mobil yang nggak ada justru dukung dia MEMANG udah pergi.

distractors.misconception: confuses deduction with obligation/expectation not met
distractors.whyFailsId: “should have” negur kewajiban yang terlewat, bukan nyimpulin dari bukti.

distractors.misconception: weakens certainty when the evidence actually supports a confident conclusion
distractors.whyFailsId: “might have” masih ragu, padahal buktinya kuat dan searah.

items.sentence: You ___ bring your passport to the local gym — a membership card is enough.

explain.why: “Needn’t” bilang sesuatu nggak diperluin, dan itu cocok sama kartu anggota yang udah cukup.
explain.rule: “Needn’t” dan “don’t have to” berarti nggak diwajibin tapi tetep boleh. “Mustn’t” berarti dilarang sama sekali.
explain.memory: “Mustn’t” berarti jangan dilakuin. “Needn’t” berarti boleh dilewatin.

distractors.misconception: treats 'mustn't' as the negation of obligation rather than prohibition
distractors.whyFailsId: artinya bawa paspor itu dilarang, padahal konteksnya cuma bilang nggak perlu.

distractors.misconception: confuses absence of necessity with negative advice
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimat ini nggak nyaranin jangan bawa paspor, cuma bilang nggak wajib.

distractors.misconception: confuses lack of requirement with lack of permission/ability
distractors.whyFailsId: nggak ada bagian konteksnya yang bilang bawa paspor nggak boleh.

items.sentence: If she ___ earlier, she wouldn't have missed the flight.

explain.why: Induk kalimatnya “wouldn’t have missed” nandain third conditional soal masa lalu yang nggak nyata. Jadi anak kalimat if-nya minta past perfect.
explain.rule: Third conditional: if + past perfect, terus would have + past participle (bentuk ke-3 kata kerja). Dipakai buat ngebayangin keadaan lampau yang nggak kejadian.
explain.memory: Dua-duanya nengok ke belakang: had ... would have ...

distractors.misconception: uses second-conditional past simple in an if-clause that needs third-conditional past perfect
distractors.whyFailsId: induk kalimat “wouldn’t have missed” nandain third conditional, bukan past simple.

distractors.misconception: duplicates 'would' in both clauses
distractors.whyFailsId: anak kalimat if dalam susunan conditional nggak pernah pakai “would”.

distractors.misconception: uses a zero/first-conditional present form for a past unreal situation
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimatnya ngomongin pengandaian masa lalu, bukan kebenaran umum.

items.sentence: If I hadn't taken that job in Berlin, I ___ fluent in German now.

explain.why: Keputusan kerjanya nggak nyata dan udah lampau, tapi kata “now” nunjuk keadaan sekarang. Jadi “wouldn't be” yang pas.
explain.rule: Mixed conditional buat sebab lampau dan akibat sekarang: if + past perfect, terus would + kata kerja dasar.
explain.memory: Sebab lampau, akibat sekarang: had done → would be.

distractors.misconception: places the result in the unreal past instead of the present
distractors.whyFailsId: akibatnya jatuh di masa lalu, padahal kata “now” minta keadaan yang dibayangin sekarang.

distractors.misconception: uses a past form without the modal required in the result clause
distractors.whyFailsId: “weren't” cuma past simple polos, jadi modal pengandai di induk kalimat ikut hilang.

distractors.misconception: repeats past perfect in the main clause
distractors.whyFailsId: past perfect itu milik anak kalimat syarat, bukan pembawa akibat di induk kalimat.

items.sentence: You won't pass the exam ___ you study harder.

explain.why: “Unless” udah berarti “if ... not”, jadi syarat belajar lebih giat nyambung tanpa kata negatif tambahan.
explain.rule: “Unless” sama dengan “if ... not”. Kata ini nggak boleh digabung sama kata negatif lain di anak kalimat yang sama.
explain.memory: “Unless” udah berarti “if not” — jangan pernah nulis “unless not”.

distractors.misconception: stacks a redundant negative onto 'unless', which is already negative in meaning
distractors.whyFailsId: kata itu udah negatif, nambah “not” bikin negatif dobel.

distractors.misconception: confuses 'if not' with 'unless' as directly interchangeable in this exact slot
distractors.whyFailsId: “if not” minta susunan yang lain, misalnya “if you don’t study harder”.

distractors.misconception: drops the negative condition entirely, reversing the sentence's logic
distractors.whyFailsId: syarat negatifnya ilang, jadi alur kalimatnya kebalik.

items.sentence: This form ___ by a licensed doctor before submission.

explain.why: Formulirnya yang kena tindakan nandatangani, dan modal “must” minta “be” + past participle biar pasifnya bener.
explain.rule: Kalimat pasif yang pakai modal disusun jadi modal + be + past participle. Contohnya “must be signed” dan “can be found”.
explain.memory: Pasif bermodal selalu butuh “be” nempel sebelum bentuk ke-3.

distractors.misconception: leaves the verb in active form after the modal
distractors.whyFailsId: susunan ini berarti formulirnya sendiri yang nandatangani, bukan yang ditandatangani.

distractors.misconception: omits the auxiliary 'be' required to form the passive after a modal
distractors.whyFailsId: pasif bermodal minta “be” sebelum bentuk ke-3 kata kerjanya.

distractors.misconception: uses the -ing form instead of the past participle
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimat pasif minta bentuk ke-3, bukan bentuk -ing “signing”.

items.sentence: To use the informal get-passive for an unexpected event: "Ugh, my bike ___ stolen outside the station last night!"

explain.why: Pasif “get” khas bahasa santai. Biasanya buat kejadian nggak enak yang datang tiba-tiba. Itu pas sama nada seruan di kalimat ini.
explain.rule: “Get” + past participle bikin pasif santai buat kejadian mendadak, nggak sengaja, atau nggak enak. “Be” + bentuk ke-3 itu bentuk baku yang netral.
explain.memory: Santai, mendadak, dan nggak enak: pakai pasif “get”.

distractors.misconception: not wrong grammatically, but ignores that the informal, exclamatory register strongly favors the 'get' passive here
distractors.whyFailsId: “was stolen” sah, tapi nada seruan “Ugh” di sini minta yang lebih santai.

distractors.misconception: misapplies present perfect auxiliary to a simple past passive event
distractors.whyFailsId: “has stolen” nggak bikin kalimat pasif di posisi ini.

distractors.misconception: uses an active-voice auxiliary in a passive construction
distractors.whyFailsId: “did” nggak bisa langsung digabung sama bentuk ke-3 buat bikin pasif.

items.sentence: She asked me, “Where do you live?” -> She asked me where ___.

explain.why: Pertanyaan langsung “Where do you live?” dilaporin jadi kayak pernyataan: “where I lived”. Kata bantu “do” hilang, subjeknya duluan.
explain.rule: Pertanyaan yang dilaporin: kata tanya + subjek + kata kerja. Kata kerjanya biasanya mundur: “live” jadi “lived”.
explain.memory: Pertanyaan yang dilaporin bunyinya kayak pernyataan, bukan pertanyaan.

distractors.misconception: keeps the question-form inversion (auxiliary before subject) inside the reported clause
distractors.whyFailsId: masih susunan tanya, padahal laporan bentuknya pernyataan.

distractors.misconception: keeps 'did' as an unnecessary emphatic auxiliary instead of a simple backshifted past verb
distractors.whyFailsId: “did” nggak dibutuhin; cukup kata kerjanya mundur jadi “lived”.

distractors.misconception: produces an ungrammatical inversion not used in either direct or reported questions in this pattern
distractors.whyFailsId: susunan kebalik kayak gini nggak ada polanya di bahasa Inggris.

items.sentence: The coach said, "Stop talking and listen!" -> The coach told the players ___.

alternates: to stop talking and to listen

explain.why: Perintah yang dilaporin pakai pola “tell”, “order”, atau “ask”, terus objeknya, terus bentuk to.
explain.rule: Perintah langsung “Do X!” dilaporin jadi “told someone to do X”. Nggak ada anak kalimat “that” dan nggak ada kata kerja yang mundur.
explain.memory: Perintah jadi “told someone TO do it”, bukan “told that they did it”.

distractors.text: that they stop talking and listen
distractors.misconception: applies the statement-reporting pattern ('that' clause) to an imperative
distractors.whyFailsId: perintah nggak dilaporin lewat anak kalimat “that”.

distractors.misconception: backshifts as if reporting a past statement rather than a command
distractors.whyFailsId: susunan pelaporannya ilang, kalimatnya jadi pernyataan lampau yang berdiri sendiri.

distractors.misconception: leaves the original imperative form unchanged, without integrating it into reported speech
distractors.whyFailsId: ini cuma ngulang perintah aslinya, belum masuk susunan pelaporan.

items.sentence: "Why don't we take the train instead?" she said. -> She ___ taking the train instead.

explain.why: “Suggested” pas sama maksud “Why don’t we ...?” dan memang nerima gerund (bentuk -ing) sebagai objeknya. Nggak ada kata ganti orang di tengahnya.
explain.rule: “Suggest” diikuti bentuk -ing atau anak kalimat that, dan nggak nerima objek orang langsung. Tell, ask, dan order diikuti objek terus bentuk to.
explain.memory: “Suggest” diikuti bentuk -ing, nggak pernah “suggested me/us to ...”.

distractors.misconception: uses a direct-instruction verb for what was actually a suggestion
distractors.whyFailsId: “told” bikin usulan halus jadi perintah, dan juga minta bentuk to.

distractors.misconception: escalates a mild suggestion into a forceful command
distractors.whyFailsId: “ordered” salah nada buat usulan yang lembut, dan minta bentuk to.

distractors.misconception: copies the object pattern of 'tell/ask' (verb + object) onto 'suggest', which doesn't take a direct personal object this way
distractors.whyFailsId: kata kerja ini nggak nerima objek orang langsung kayak “us” di tengahnya.

items.sentence: ___ elephants we saw at Ragunan Zoo yesterday were huge.

explain.why: Ada keterangan “we saw at Ragunan Zoo yesterday”, jadi gajahnya udah jelas yang mana. Benda yang udah jelas pakai “The”.
explain.rule: “The” buat benda yang udah sama-sama diketahui. Pernyataan umum soal semua gajah malah tanpa artikel: “Elephants are big”.
explain.memory: Udah tahu yang mana: pakai “the”. Semua secara umum: tanpa artikel.

distractors.misconception: applies a singular indefinite article to a plural noun
distractors.whyFailsId: “a” buat satu benda, padahal “elephants” jamak.

distractors.misconception: applies a singular indefinite article to a plural noun and ignores the consonant sound
distractors.whyFailsId: “an” buat satu benda bunyi vokal, padahal “elephants” jamak.

items.sentence: We don't have ___ chairs for all the guests.

explain.why: “Chairs” bisa dihitung satu-satu dan bentuknya jamak. Jadi “many” yang pas di kalimat negatif ini.
explain.rule: Benda jamak yang bisa dihitung satu-satu pakai many atau few. Benda yang nggak bisa dihitung satu-satu pakai much atau little.
explain.memory: Bisa dihitung: many atau few. Nggak bisa dihitung: much atau little.

distractors.misconception: applies the uncountable-noun quantifier to a countable plural noun
distractors.whyFailsId: “chairs” bisa dihitung satu-satu, “much” minta yang nggak bisa.

distractors.misconception: applies the uncountable-noun quantifier ('little') to a countable plural noun, and also confuses scarcity type
distractors.whyFailsId: “little” buat benda yang nggak bisa dihitung, kayak air.

distractors.misconception: adds an unnecessary partitive 'of' without a following determiner, and still misapplies 'much' to a countable noun
distractors.whyFailsId: “much of” minta frasa benda yang udah tertentu.

items.sentence: I clearly remember ___ the front door before we left this morning.

explain.why: Bentuk -ing “locking” nyatain ingatan atas tindakan yang udah kelar, dan itu pas sama “this morning”.
explain.rule: “Remember” + -ing berarti inget sesuatu yang udah kejadian. “Remember” + to berarti nggak lupa ngerjain sesuatu nanti.
explain.memory: “Remember doing” itu ingatan lampau; “remember to do” itu tugas nanti.

distractors.misconception: applies the 'future duty' pattern ('remember to do') to a sentence that is actually recalling a completed past action
distractors.whyFailsId: “remember to lock” berarti jangan lupa nanti, padahal kalimatnya inget kejadian pagi itu.

distractors.misconception: uses the bare infinitive, which isn't a valid pattern after 'remember' in either meaning
distractors.whyFailsId: “remember” cuma diikuti bentuk -ing atau bentuk to, nggak pernah bentuk dasar.

distractors.misconception: adds an unnecessary obligation phrase not supported by the sentence's meaning
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimatnya inget tindakan nguncinya, bukan inget adanya kewajiban ngunci.

items.sentence: She left work early ___ time to prepare for the interview.

explain.why: “To have time to prepare” bilang alasan dia balik awal. Itu memang tugas bentuk to.
explain.rule: Bentuk to buat tujuan jawab pertanyaan “kenapa”. Bentuk -ing nyusul setelah kata depan, kayak “interested in”, bukan buat nyatain tujuan.
explain.memory: Tujuan cukup “to” plus kata kerja, tanpa kata depan.

distractors.misconception: misreads the sentence as needing a preposition + gerund structure instead of an infinitive of purpose
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimatnya nyatain kenapa dia balik awal, bukan tempelan kata depan.

distractors.misconception: mixes a preposition with a to-infinitive, a combination that isn't standard in English
distractors.whyFailsId: dalam Bahasa Inggris, “for to” nggak berdiri di depan kata kerja dasar.

distractors.misconception: drops the purpose marker entirely, leaving a bare gerund with no clear grammatical link to the main clause
distractors.whyFailsId: tanpa kata pengantar, hubungan tujuannya ilang dan susunannya nggak lengkap.

items.sentence: That's the author ___ latest novel just won an international award.

explain.why: “Whose” negesin “latest novel” itu punya penulisnya, jadi kepemilikannya nyambung.
explain.rule: “Whose” itu kata penghubung kepemilikan. Dipakai sebelum kata benda buat nunjukin benda itu punya orang yang baru disebut.
explain.memory: “Whose” berarti punya; “who’s” berarti who is atau who has.

distractors.misconception: confuses the contraction 'who's' (who is / who has) with the possessive relative pronoun 'whose'
distractors.whyFailsId: “who’s” berarti who is atau who has, bukan bentuk kepemilikan.

distractors.misconception: uses the subject relative pronoun without showing the required possessive relationship
distractors.whyFailsId: “who” sendirian nggak bisa nunjukin bukunya punya penulisnya.

distractors.misconception: uses the non-personal relative pronoun for a person (the author)
distractors.whyFailsId: “which” nunjuk benda dan bukan orang, jadi nggak bisa balik ke “the author”.

items.sentence: This laptop is ___ the one I had before — both take exactly ten seconds to start up.

explain.why: Dua laptop butuh waktu yang sama persis, sepuluh detik. Jadi cuma bentuk setara “as fast as” yang cocok.
explain.rule: Pola as + kata sifat + as bilang dua hal setara. Bentuk “lebih” (comparative) bareng “than” bilang ada selisih.
explain.memory: Sama persis berarti nggak ada selisih, jadi pakai as ... as.

distractors.misconception: defaults to the comparative form even though the context implies equality, not difference
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimatnya bilang waktunya sama persis, bukan ada yang lebih cepat.

distractors.misconception: confuses a two-item comparison with a superlative among three or more items
distractors.whyFailsId: cuma dua laptop yang dibandingin, ini bentuk “paling”.

distractors.misconception: applies the periphrastic 'more + adjective' pattern to a short one-syllable adjective that takes '-er'
distractors.whyFailsId: “fast” itu kata sifat pendek, bentuknya pakai -er.

items.sentence: Which completion best expresses a gradual increase that keeps continuing? As the deadline approached, the team's schedule became ___.

explain.why: “As the deadline approached” nandain peningkatan yang bertahap dan terus berlanjut. Comparative ganda “busier and busier” yang nyatain makna itu.
explain.rule: Pola bentuk lebih + and + bentuk lebih nyatain perubahan yang jalan terus. Contohnya “busier and busier” atau “more and more difficult”.
explain.memory: Perubahan yang jalan terus nggandain bentuk lebihnya.

distractors.misconception: treats a continuous, ongoing change as a single fixed-point comparison
distractors.whyFailsId: “busier than before” bener, tapi cuma bandingin sama satu titik waktu sebelumnya.

distractors.misconception: confuses a progressive change over time with a superlative ranking among multiple items
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimatnya nggak bandingin jadwal ini sama jadwal lain.

distractors.misconception: uses a single comparative with 'more' for a short adjective, and frames it as a comparison to a norm rather than ongoing change
distractors.whyFailsId: “busy” biasanya pakai akhiran -er, bukan “more”.

items.sentence: You look exhausted. ___ you sleep at all last night?

explain.why: “Didn’t you sleep ...” nunjukin heran atas wajah yang keliatan capek. Kata bantunya lampau, jadi cocok sama “last night”.
explain.rule: Pertanyaan negatif kayak “Didn’t you ...?” sering nunjukin heran atau ngarep persetujuan. Kata bantunya tetep harus cocok sama acuan waktu kalimatnya.
explain.memory: Wajah capek plus “last night” minta pertanyaan “didn’t”, bukan “do”.

distractors.misconception: uses a neutral positive question form, missing the speaker's implied surprise/assumption
distractors.whyFailsId: pertanyaan “Do” yang polos ngilangin nada heran di konteksnya.

distractors.misconception: uses present-tense negative auxiliary in a context that requires the past tense to match 'last night'
distractors.whyFailsId: “last night” maku pertanyaannya di masa lalu, kata bantunya jadi bentrok.

distractors.misconception: uses the 'be' auxiliary instead of the 'do' auxiliary needed for the main verb 'sleep'
distractors.whyFailsId: “sleep” itu kata kerja utama biasa, bukan urusan kata bantu be.

items.sentence: Direct question: “Where is the nearest pharmacy?” -> Excuse me, could you tell me where ___?

explain.why: Di dalam “could you tell me ...”, urutannya jadi kayak pernyataan: “the nearest pharmacy is”. Nggak dibalik jadi “is the nearest pharmacy”.
explain.rule: Pertanyaan sopan: kata tanya + subjek + kata kerja. “Is” tetap present karena letak apotek nggak berubah.
explain.memory: Pertanyaan sopan yang nyempil: subjek dulu, kata kerja nyusul.

distractors.misconception: keeps direct-question inversion (verb before subject) inside the embedded clause
distractors.whyFailsId: masih susunan tanya langsung, padahal di kalimat sopan subjek duluan.

distractors.misconception: unnecessarily backshifts to past tense when the pharmacy's existence is a current, general fact
distractors.whyFailsId: “was” bikin lampau, padahal letak apotek fakta sekarang.

items.sentence: In 2010, nobody guessed that the small startup ___ the entire industry within a decade.

explain.why: “Would” + kata kerja dasar nyatain kejadian yang saat itu masih di depan kalau diukur dari 2010. Diceritain dari sudut yang lebih belakangan.
explain.rule: Masa depan yang dilihat dari masa lalu pakai would atau was going to + kata kerja. Buat nggambarin apa yang nyusul sesudah satu titik lampau.
explain.memory: Titik lampau ditambah “would” berarti masa depan yang sekarang udah kejadian.

distractors.misconception: confusing future-in-the-past with past continuous background action
distractors.whyFailsId: past continuous nggambarin tindakan yang masih jalan di titik lampau itu.

distractors.misconception: using present-tense future modal inside a past narrative frame
distractors.whyFailsId: kata kunci “In 2010” maku kalimatnya ke masa lalu, jadi “will” nggak sejalan.

distractors.misconception: collapsing future-in-the-past into simple past
distractors.whyFailsId: past simple nyatain perubahannya sebagai fakta lampau biasa, jadi sudut pandangnya ilang.

items.sentence: Which completion foregrounds the accumulated duration of the studying as the cause of his red eyes? His eyes were red because he ___ all night for the exam.

explain.why: Past perfect continuous nonjolin lamanya belajar sebagai sebab langsung dari mata yang memerah.
explain.rule: Past perfect continuous bentuknya had been + kata kerja -ing. Dipakai buat durasi sebelum satu titik lampau, terutama kalau durasi itu nerangin akibat yang kelihatan.
explain.memory: Mata memerah butuh sebab berdurasi: “had been -ing”.

distractors.misconception: treating past perfect simple as sufficient for any earlier past event
distractors.whyFailsId: bahasanya bener dan waktunya lebih awal, tapi nekanin belajarnya udah tuntas, bukan lamanya.

distractors.misconception: using simple past for a state that must be shown as prior to another past moment
distractors.whyFailsId: bahasanya bener, tapi cuma nglaporin faktanya, nggak nonjolin lamanya belajar.

distractors.misconception: confusing past continuous with past perfect continuous
distractors.whyFailsId: past continuous naruh tindakannya bareng kejadian lampau lain, bukan jelas mendahuluinya.

items.sentence: Which completion gives the strongest urgent warning tied to the stated consequence? You ___ leave now — if you miss this train, there isn't another one until tomorrow.

explain.why: “Had better” dipakai buat nasihat mendesak yang akibat buruknya disebut jelas.
explain.rule: “Had better” plus kata kerja dasar berarti nasihat kuat buat keadaan tertentu. Bentuk ini bawa akibat buruk kalau diabaikan.
explain.memory: Kereta terakhir sampai besok, berarti “had better” hari ini.

distractors.misconception: treating general advice modal as equally strong as urgent-consequence modal
distractors.whyFailsId: nasihat umum, tanpa desakan akibat yang ditandai anak kalimat “if”.

distractors.misconception: using a possibility modal where obligation/urgency is meant
distractors.whyFailsId: cuma nawarin pilihan, bukan desakan kuat dari akibat yang disebut.

distractors.misconception: using a modal of weak possibility for a directive
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang nggak pasti soal kejadian nanti, bukan nasihat mendesak.

items.sentence: I'm not sure where Sam is, and I have no idea what the roads are like — he ___ still be stuck in traffic.

explain.why: “Might” bilang tebakan yang masih ragu soal keadaan sekarang, dan itu cocok sama “I’m not sure”.
explain.rule: “May”, “might”, dan “could” plus kata kerja dasar bilang kemungkinan lemah soal sekarang. “Must” bilang kesimpulan kuat, “will” bilang ramalan yang yakin.
explain.memory: “Not sure” pasangannya “might”, bukan “will”.

distractors.misconception: using the confident future/prediction modal for uncertain present speculation
distractors.whyFailsId: negesin keyakinan, padahal “I’m not sure” bilang sebaliknya.

distractors.misconception: using the strong-deduction modal where only weak possibility is intended
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang kesimpulan yakin dari bukti, jauh lebih kuat dari tebakan.

distractors.misconception: using 'can' for a specific present possibility about one situation
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang kemungkinan umum, bukan tebakan soal keadaan sekarang.

items.sentence: He's exhausted today — he ___ up so late watching movies last night.

explain.why: “Shouldn’t have stayed” negur tindakan yang memang kejadian, yaitu begadang, dan itu penyebab kelelahannya hari ini.
explain.rule: “Should have” + bentuk ke-3 nyesalin kebaikan yang nggak jadi dilakuin. “Shouldn’t have” + bentuk ke-3 negur tindakan nyata yang ternyata keliru.
explain.memory: Kelelahan hari ini berarti tadi malam memang begadang, jadi “shouldn’t have”.

distractors.misconception: missing the negation needed for criticizing a completed unwise action
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk ini malah bilang dia nggak begadang, padahal konteksnya bilang sebaliknya.

distractors.misconception: using present-form advice modal instead of past-regret structure
distractors.whyFailsId: begadangnya udah kelar dan lagi dinilai dari belakang, jadi “should” bentuk present nggak pas.

distractors.misconception: confusing third conditional result clause with a past-regret judgement
distractors.whyFailsId: “wouldn’t have” punya hasil pengandaian, bukan teguran langsung atas tindakan nyata.

items.sentence: ___ known about the delay, I would have booked a later flight.

explain.why: “Had I known” itu bentuk formal terbalik dari “If I had known”, biasa dipakai di third conditional ragam formal.
explain.rule: Pengandaian formal bisa dibalik: Had + subjek + past participle, tanpa “if”. Artinya sama kayak if + subjek + had + past participle.
explain.memory: Buang “if”, balik urutannya: “Had I known” sama dengan “If I had known”.

distractors.misconception: mixing formal inversion with the conjunction 'if' at the same time
distractors.whyFailsId: pembalikan formal udah gantiin “if”, jadi majang keduanya sekaligus bikin susunannya nggak sah.

distractors.misconception: using normal subject-verb order, missing the inversion signal
distractors.whyFailsId: tanpa “if”, urutan biasa “I had known” nggak bisa berdiri sendiri sebagai anak kalimat pengandaian.

distractors.misconception: using the result-clause auxiliary structure at the start of the if-clause
distractors.whyFailsId: “would” itu milik anak kalimat hasil, bukan milik anak kalimat syarat yang minta “had”.

items.sentence: The bridge was closed for repairs; otherwise, the trip ___ much shorter.

explain.why: “Otherwise” di sini nyimpen makna “kalau jembatannya nggak ditutup”. Jadi hasilnya minta bentuk third conditional.
explain.rule: “Otherwise” bisa nyimpen syarat yang nggak nyata. Anak kalimat sesudahnya pakai bentuk hasil pengandaian sesuai waktu syarat tersembunyi itu.
explain.memory: “Otherwise” itu “if not” yang tersembunyi, jadi sering minta “would have + past participle”.

distractors.misconception: reading 'otherwise' as a simple future contrast marker
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimatnya ngomongin hasil lampau yang cuma dibayangin, bukan kejadian nyata di masa depan.

distractors.misconception: treating the implied condition as a real past fact rather than a hypothetical one
distractors.whyFailsId: past simple bakal ngeklaim perjalanannya memang lebih singkat, padahal jembatannya ditutup.

distractors.misconception: ignoring the past time frame set by 'was closed'
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk present nggak cocok sama keadaan lampau yang cuma dibayangin di kalimat ini.

items.sentence: ___ that the ancient city was destroyed by an earthquake, though no written records survive.

explain.why: “It is believed that ...” itu bentuk baku pasif pelaporan tanpa pelaku. Dipakai buat anggapan yang luas dianut tapi nggak jelas sumbernya.
explain.rule: Pelaporan pasif tanpa pelaku: It + is atau was + past participle + anak kalimat that. Subjek semu “it” selalu tunggal.
explain.memory: Tanpa sumber yang disebut dan bernada resmi: “It is believed that ...”.

distractors.misconception: using active voice with a vague 'they' plus an incorrect continuous form for a general belief
distractors.whyFailsId: “believe” biasanya nggak dipakai bentuk continuous buat anggapan umum.

distractors.misconception: treating 'it' as an active subject capable of believing
distractors.whyFailsId: “it” di sini cuma subjek semu dan nggak bisa yakin sama sesuatu.

distractors.misconception: dropping the required dummy subject 'it' from the impersonal passive pattern
distractors.whyFailsId: tanpa “it” di depan, kalimatnya kehilangan subjeknya.

items.sentence: The new policy is expected ___ next month, though the exact date hasn't been confirmed.

explain.why: Kebijakan itulah yang kena tindakan ngumumin, jadi bentuk to pasif “to be announced” diwajibin sesudah “is expected”.
explain.rule: Bentuk to pasif itu to be + past participle. Dipakai kalau subjek dari bentuk to itu nerima tindakannya, sering sesudah expect, believe, atau report.
explain.memory: Kebijakannya diumumin, bukan ngumumin: “to be announced”.

distractors.misconception: using active infinitive when the subject (the policy) cannot perform the announcing itself
distractors.whyFailsId: “to announce” bikin kebijakan itu jadi pihak yang ngumumin.

distractors.misconception: using a gerund where an infinitive pattern after 'expected' is required
distractors.whyFailsId: “expected” diikuti pelengkap bentuk to, bukan bentuk -ing.

distractors.misconception: adding continuous aspect to the passive infinitive unnecessarily
distractors.whyFailsId: “to be announcing” bikin pengumuman sekali jadi kedengeran kayak proses panjang.

items.sentence: On Monday, Maria said, 'I'll finish the report today.' A week later, reporting this, you'd say: Maria said she would finish the report ___.

explain.why: “That day” nunjuk balik ke hari yang dimaksud Maria, yaitu Senin, dari sudut pandang sekarang.
explain.rule: Di kalimat pelaporan, kata waktu dan tempat ikut geser: “today” jadi “that day”, “here” jadi “there”, “tomorrow” jadi “the next day”.
explain.memory: Kata kerjanya mundur, “today” pun ikut geser jadi “that day”.

distractors.misconception: leaving the original deictic time word unchanged despite the shift in reporting time
distractors.whyFailsId: kata itu cuma masuk akal di hari Senin waktu Maria ngomong.

distractors.misconception: misreading the original 'today' as if it referred to the day after speaking
distractors.whyFailsId: kata aslinya “today”, artinya hari yang sama, bukan besoknya.

distractors.misconception: producing an incomplete deictic shift missing the demonstrative
distractors.whyFailsId: “the day” doang belum utuh, kata penunjuknya kelupaan.

items.sentence: Can you pass me ___ books on the shelf over there?

explain.why: “Books” jumlahnya banyak. “Over there” bilang bendanya jauh. “Those” pas buat dua-duanya.
explain.rule: this buat satu benda dekat. that buat satu benda jauh. these buat banyak benda dekat. those buat banyak benda jauh.
explain.memory: Banyak dan jauh: “those books over there”.

distractors.misconception: using a singular near demonstrative with a plural, distant noun
distractors.whyFailsId: cuma buat satu benda yang letaknya dekat.

distractors.misconception: correctly matching distance but ignoring plural agreement
distractors.whyFailsId: jaraknya udah pas, tapi cuma buat satu benda.

distractors.misconception: correctly matching plural but ignoring the distance cue
distractors.whyFailsId: jumlahnya udah pas, tapi nunjuk benda yang dekat.

items.sentence: The meeting has been put ___ until next Thursday because two directors are traveling.

explain.why: “Put off” khusus berarti nunda sesuatu ke waktu yang lebih belakangan, cocok sama “until next Thursday”.
explain.rule: Partikel di kata kerja gabungan (phrasal verb) nggak bisa gantian. Kata kerja yang sama plus partikel beda bisa bikin makna yang jauh.
explain.memory: “Put off” sebuah rapat berarti ndorong jadwalnya lebih jauh ke depan.

distractors.misconception: confusing 'put down' (to set something down / write something / criticize) with 'put off' (postpone)
distractors.whyFailsId: “put down” berarti naruh, nulis, atau ngerendahin orang.

distractors.misconception: confusing 'put up' (to erect / accommodate / tolerate) with 'put off' (postpone)
distractors.whyFailsId: “put up” berarti mendirikan, masang, atau nahan keadaan.

distractors.misconception: confusing 'put away' (to store something) with 'put off' (postpone)
distractors.whyFailsId: “put away” berarti nyimpen atau ngerapiin sesuatu.

items.sentence: We squeezed ___ the narrow gap in the fence.

explain.why: Celah pagar itu sempit dan tertutup, dimasuki dari satu sisi. “Through” nandain gerak masuk lalu keluar di sisi lain.
explain.rule: “Through” nembus ruang tertutup. “Across” nyeberangi bidang datar terbuka. “Along” nyusuri panjangnya sesuatu. “Over” lewat di atasnya.
explain.memory: Celah punya bagian dalam, jadi ditembus pakai “through”.

distractors.misconception: using the flat-open-surface preposition for an enclosed three-dimensional space
distractors.whyFailsId: “across” nyeberangi bidang datar, celah nggak punya bidang.

distractors.misconception: using the linear-edge preposition (following a line such as a river or street) for movement inside an enclosed space
distractors.whyFailsId: “along” nyusuri panjangnya, bukan nembus ke sisi lain.

distractors.misconception: using the above-and-across preposition for movement inside a space, not above it
distractors.whyFailsId: “over” lewat bagian atas pagar, bukan celahnya.

items.sentence: The coffee was too hot ___ right away, so she waited a few minutes.

explain.why: “Too hot to drink” pakai pola baku “too” + kata sifat + bentuk “to”. Kadar panasnya bikin minum langsung nggak mungkin.
explain.rule: Pola “too” + kata sifat + bentuk “to” bilang kadarnya kelewatan. Akibatnya satu tindakan nggak bisa dilakukan. Kalau pelakunya perlu disebut, sisipin “for” + orangnya sebelum bentuk “to”.
explain.memory: Habis “too” + kata sifat, selalu nyusul “to”.

distractors.misconception: using a gerund where the too/enough + adjective structure requires a to-infinitive
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk -ing nggak muat di pola tetap ini.

distractors.misconception: inserting an unnecessary preposition before the verb form
distractors.whyFailsId: “for” nggak boleh nempel langsung di depan kata kerjanya.

distractors.misconception: using the bare infinitive instead of the required to-infinitive
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar telanjang belum lengkap buat pola tetap ini.

items.sentence: This is the colleague ___ I was speaking earlier — a very formal way to phrase it.

explain.why: “With whom” itu susunan formal yang bener: kata depan diikuti bentuk objek “whom” buat orang.
explain.rule: Di Bahasa Inggris formal, kata depan yang dimajuin wajib diikuti “whom” buat orang, bukan “who”. Ragam santai malah naruh kata depannya di akhir bareng “who”.
explain.memory: Kata depan di depan minta “whom”, bukan “who”.

distractors.misconception: using subject-form 'who' after a fronted preposition, which requires the object form
distractors.whyFailsId: kata depan yang persis di depan kata penghubung minta bentuk objek, bukan bentuk subjek.

distractors.misconception: reverses the preposition-pronoun order, putting 'with' directly after 'who' mid-clause
distractors.whyFailsId: urutannya kebalik, “with” jatuh persis sesudah “who” di tengah kalimat, dan itu nggak sah.

distractors.misconception: using the non-personal relative pronoun for a person
distractors.whyFailsId: “which” nunjuk benda. “Colleague” itu orang, jadi butuh kata penghubung buat orang.

items.sentence: This recipe uses ___ eggs than the one my grandmother used to make.

explain.why: “Eggs” itu benda jamak yang bisa dihitung satu-satu. Bentuk perbandingan jumlahnya “fewer”.
explain.rule: “Fewer” buat benda jamak yang bisa dihitung satu-satu. “Less” buat benda yang nggak bisa dihitung satu-satu. Di percakapan santai “less” makin sering kedengeran, tapi pemakaian baku tetap bedain keduanya.
explain.memory: Telur bisa dihitung satu-satu, jadi pakai “fewer”.

distractors.misconception: applying the uncountable-noun comparative to a countable plural noun
distractors.whyFailsId: “less” disediain buat benda yang nggak bisa dihitung satu-satu.

distractors.misconception: using the base uncountable quantifier instead of its comparative form
distractors.whyFailsId: “little” bukan bentuk perbandingan sama sekali.

distractors.misconception: intensifying the wrong (uncountable) comparative rather than switching to the countable form
distractors.whyFailsId: nambah “much” nggak nyentuh salah pasang keterhitungannya.

items.sentence: I looked everywhere, but I didn't find ___ in the drawer.

explain.why: “Anything” nggak bawa arti negatif sendiri. Jadi dia cocok dipasangin “didn’t” yang udah negatif.
explain.rule: Inggris baku cuma pakai satu kata negatif per kalimat. Kata kerja negatif dipasangin kata berawalan any, bukan berawalan no.
explain.memory: Satu kata negatif per kalimat: “didn’t ... anything”, bukan “didn’t ... nothing”.

distractors.misconception: combining a negated verb ('didn't') with a negative pronoun, creating a non-standard double negative
distractors.whyFailsId: “didn’t find nothing” bawa dua kata negatif sekaligus.

distractors.misconception: using a positive indefinite pronoun that contradicts the negative context
distractors.whyFailsId: “something” bilang ada benda yang ketemu, padahal kalimatnya nyangkal.

distractors.misconception: incorrectly splitting the compound negative pronoun into two words
distractors.whyFailsId: “nothing” itu satu kata, dipenggal jadi nggak baku.

items.sentence: A: 'I don't really enjoy horror movies.' B: '___ I. They give me nightmares.'

explain.why: Ucapan “A” negatif lewat “don’t enjoy”. Jadi persetujuannya juga harus bentuk negatif, yaitu “Neither do I”.
explain.rule: “So” + kata bantu + subjek nyetujuin pernyataan positif. “Neither” atau “Nor” + kata bantu + subjek nyetujuin pernyataan negatif.
explain.memory: Ada “don’t”, berarti persetujuannya juga negatif.

distractors.misconception: using the positive agreement structure to agree with a negative statement
distractors.whyFailsId: “so do I” buat nyetujuin pernyataan positif.

distractors.misconception: combining the wrong polarity structure with the wrong subject-verb agreement form
distractors.whyFailsId: “does” nggak cocok sama subjek “I”.

distractors.misconception: confusing 'either' (used with 'not...either' at the end of a clause) with the fronted 'neither' agreement structure
distractors.whyFailsId: “either” dipakai di pola “I don’t either”.

items.sentence: According to the timetable, the train ___ at 6:45, so we should leave home by 6:15.

explain.why: Kalimatnya nyebut “according to the timetable”, jadi jadwalnya resmi. Jadwal resmi ngomong pakai present simple.
explain.rule: Present simple dipakai buat kejadian nanti yang udah dipatok jadwal, acara, atau kalender. Bentuk ini nggak bergantung pada niat pribadi siapa pun.
explain.memory: Jadwal ngomong pakai present simple.

distractors.misconception: using present continuous, associated with personal arrangements, for a fixed external timetable
distractors.whyFailsId: present continuous biasanya nyebut janji yang dibikin orang.

distractors.misconception: using 'going to' for intention/prediction rather than an externally fixed schedule
distractors.whyFailsId: “going to” nyebut rencana atau ramalan dari tanda-tanda sekarang.

distractors.misconception: using future perfect, which describes completion before a reference point, not the scheduled departure itself
distractors.whyFailsId: future perfect nyebut keretanya udah jalan sebelum satu waktu tertentu.

items.sentence: Which completion emphasizes the duration accumulating up to the deadline rather than merely the fact of completion? By the time she retires next year, Maria ____ at this company for over two decades.

explain.why: Future perfect continuous bentuknya will have been + kata kerja -ing. Bentuk itu nonjolin lamanya kegiatan yang jalan terus sampai satu titik di masa depan.
explain.rule: Pakai will have been + kata kerja -ing kalau lamanya waktu dihitung sampai satu titik tertentu di masa depan.
explain.memory: Lamanya waktu plus batas di masa depan: will have been + kata kerja -ing.

distractors.misconception: Confuses future continuous (in-progress at a moment) with future perfect continuous (duration up to a point).
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk ini nggambarin tindakan yang jalan di satu saat, bukan lamanya waktu yang numpuk.

distractors.misconception: Confuses future perfect simple (completion/result) with future perfect continuous (ongoing duration emphasis).
distractors.whyFailsId: bahasanya bener, tapi ia nglaporin fakta yang udah tuntas, bukan lamanya yang numpuk.

distractors.misconception: Treats the sentence as a plain future prediction, ignoring the 'by the time' anchor.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk masa depan sederhana nggak nyambungin lamanya tindakan itu ke titik acuannya.

items.sentence: When I arrived at the station, the train ____ already, so I had to wait for the next one.

explain.why: Past perfect nandain keberangkatan keretanya udah kelar sebelum penuturnya tiba, jadi itu kejadian yang lebih dulu.
explain.rule: Pakai past perfect buat kejadian yang lebih dulu di antara dua kejadian lampau, pas urutannya perlu ditegasin.
explain.memory: Kejadian lampau yang lebih dulu pakai had + past participle (bentuk ke-3 kata kerja).

distractors.misconception: Treats both events as equally sequential in past simple.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk ini nggak nandain keretanya berangkat sebelum dia tiba.

distractors.misconception: Confuses past continuous (in-progress) with an already-completed prior event.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk ini bilang keretanya masih dalam proses berangkat saat itu.

distractors.misconception: Uses present perfect, mixing a present-relevance tense into a past narrative.
distractors.whyFailsId: present perfect nggak bisa digabung sama kerangka waktu lampau “when I arrived”.

items.sentence: This house ____ to my grandparents; it has been in the family for fifty years.

explain.why: “Belong” bilang keadaan kepemilikan yang menetap. Jadi present simple yang dibutuhin, walaupun konteksnya sekarang.
explain.rule: Kata kerja keadaan kayak belong, own, believe, dan know biasanya nggak pakai bentuk -ing.
explain.memory: Keadaan nggak berproses: belong, own, dan believe tanpa -ing.

distractors.misconception: Assumes present time always requires present continuous.
distractors.whyFailsId: “belong” itu keadaan menetap, bukan proses yang jalan.

distractors.misconception: Shifts to past tense despite the present-relevance context.
distractors.whyFailsId: rumahnya masih milik mereka sampai sekarang.

distractors.misconception: Forces a passive continuous structure onto an intransitive stative verb.
distractors.whyFailsId: “belong” nggak pernah dipakai dalam bentuk pasif.

items.sentence: Which completion neutrally states an available past opportunity without criticizing the decision? You ____ the job — they offered it to you, but you turned it down.

explain.why: “Could have taken” bilang pekerjaan itu beneran tersedia sebagai pilihan di masa lalu, tapi nggak diambil.
explain.rule: Could have + bentuk ke-3 berarti kemungkinan di masa lalu yang nggak jadi kejadian.
explain.memory: “Could have” berarti pintunya kebuka, tapi nggak ada yang lewat.

distractors.misconception: Confuses missed opportunity with retrospective advice/criticism.
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimatnya nggak negur pilihannya, cuma nyebut peluangnya ada dan ditolak.

distractors.misconception: Confuses expressing a past possibility with reporting a completed achieved ability.
distractors.whyFailsId: “were able to” nyiratin tindakannya beneran dilakuin, bentrok sama “you turned it down”.

distractors.misconception: Uses present modal for a past hypothetical situation.
distractors.whyFailsId: semua kejadiannya udah lampau, jadi modal bentuk present nggak selaras waktunya.

items.sentence: For the conventionally most formal wording in an official notice: Visitors ___ enter the laboratory only when accompanied by staff.

explain.why: Soalnya nyebut “official notice”, jadi yang diminta ragam paling resmi. “May” modal izin yang lazim di ragam itu.
explain.rule: Pakai “may” buat izin di ragam resmi. “Can” biasa dipakai buat izin di percakapan santai. Dua-duanya sah, cuma ragamnya beda.
explain.memory: Pengumuman resmi pakai modal resmi.

distractors.misconception: Assumes 'can' is equally acceptable in formal written permission notices.
distractors.whyFailsId: “can” kedengeran terlalu santai buat pengumuman resmi.

distractors.misconception: Uses the past/tentative form of 'can' for a present-tense rule.
distractors.whyFailsId: “could” melunak jadi pengandaian atau makna lampau.

distractors.misconception: Confuses formal permission with weak possibility.
distractors.whyFailsId: “might” nyebut kemungkinan yang belum pasti.

items.sentence: ____ resign now, the whole project would collapse.

explain.why: “Were I to resign” itu bentuk formal terbalik dari “If I were to resign”, dengan “were” dimajuin ke depan.
explain.rule: Second conditional yang formal bisa dibalik jadi Were + subjek + bentuk to, gantiin “if”.
explain.memory: “Were I to ...” itu bentuk formal terbalik dari “If I were to ...”.

distractors.misconception: Adds 'if' to a structure that already signals conditionality through inversion.
distractors.whyFailsId: pengandaian terbalik udah gantiin “if”, jadi majang dua-duanya bikin susunannya nggak sah.

distractors.misconception: Drops the inversion, leaving a non-inverted fragment without 'if'.
distractors.whyFailsId: tanpa “if” dan tanpa kata kerja di depan, anak kalimatnya nggak ditandai sebagai pengandaian.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'was' instead of the subjunctive 'were' required in formal hypothetical inversion.
distractors.whyFailsId: second conditional terbalik yang formal minta “were”, bukan “was”, apa pun subjeknya.

items.sentence: I'll call you as soon as the train ___.

explain.why: “Arrives” itu present simple. Bentuk itu yang biasa nyusul “as soon as” walau kedatangannya nanti.
explain.rule: Kata penghubung waktunya bisa “when”, “as soon as”, “before”, “after”, “until”, atau “once”. Di anak kalimat waktu itu, pakai present simple. Bentuk “will” biasanya ditaruh di induk kalimatnya.
explain.memory: Habis “as soon as”, present simple tetep bermakna nanti.

distractors.misconception: duplicates future marking inside the time clause
distractors.whyFailsId: “will” biasanya ditaruh di induk kalimatnya.

distractors.misconception: shifts the time clause into a completed past event
distractors.whyFailsId: menelepon dan kedatangannya sama-sama masih nanti.

distractors.misconception: treats a real future sequence as hypothetical or future-in-the-past
distractors.whyFailsId: nggak ada syarat nggak nyata atau bingkai lampau di kalimatnya.

items.sentence: We ___ our roof repaired last week after the storm damaged it.

explain.why: “Had” pas sama kata kunci lampau “last week” dan nglengkapin kerangka nyuruh di sekitar “our roof repaired”. Semuanya dalam bentuk lampau.
explain.rule: Pola causative: subjek + have atau get + objek + past participle. Artinya ngatur biar sebuah jasa dikerjain orang lain.
explain.memory: Pasif biasa pakai was atau were; nyuruh orang lain pakai had + bendanya + past participle.

distractors.misconception: Treats the sentence as simple passive ('the roof was repaired') rather than causative.
distractors.whyFailsId: “we were our roof repaired” nggak sah; pasif biasa bunyinya “our roof was repaired”.

distractors.misconception: Mixes present perfect passive auxiliary into a past-time causative sentence.
distractors.whyFailsId: “have been” nggak cocok sama kata kunci waktu lampau “last week”.

distractors.misconception: Attempts simple past passive but misapplies subject-verb agreement and structure.
distractors.whyFailsId: “we was” salah kesesuaian subjeknya, dan pasif biasa juga nggak nangkep makna ngatur.

items.sentence: The suspect ____ have left the country before the investigation began.

explain.why: “The suspect is believed to have left ...” itu pola pasif berorang: orangnya, terus is believed, terus bentuk to.
explain.rule: Pasif pelaporan berorang: subjek + is atau are + believed, thought, atau said + bentuk to, bukan “that”.
explain.memory: Orangnya + is believed + to, bukan “that”.

distractors.misconception: Blends the personal passive subject pattern with the impersonal 'that'-clause pattern.
distractors.whyFailsId: begitu orangnya jadi subjek, lanjutannya wajib bentuk to, bukan “that”.

distractors.misconception: Adds a redundant impersonal 'it' when the sentence already has a personal subject.
distractors.whyFailsId: “it” ngegandain peran subjek yang udah diisi “the suspect”, jadi ada dua subjek.

distractors.misconception: Omits the passive auxiliary 'is' entirely.
distractors.whyFailsId: tanpa “is”, nggak ada kata kerja bertense yang nopang susunan pasifnya.

items.sentence: He asked me, “Did you lock the door?” -> He asked me ___ the door.

explain.why: “Whether I had locked” nandain pertanyaan “yes” atau “no” yang dilaporin. Urutannya kayak pernyataan, dan tindakan yang lebih dulu ikut digeser.
explain.rule: Pertanyaan “yes” atau “no” yang dilaporin: “ask” + “if” atau “whether” + subjek + kata kerja. Pembalikan khas pertanyaan langsung nggak dipertahanin.
explain.memory: Pelaporan “yes” atau “no” pakai “whether” + subjek + kata kerja.

distractors.misconception: keeps direct-question inversion and omits if/whether
distractors.whyFailsId: pertanyaan yang dilaporin pakai urutan pernyataan.

distractors.misconception: uses 'that' for a yes/no reported question
distractors.whyFailsId: “that” buat pernyataan yang dilaporin.

distractors.misconception: adds whether but retains auxiliary-subject inversion
distractors.whyFailsId: kata bantunya masih dibalik di depan subjeknya.

items.sentence: To express attendance for the institution's normal purpose, not movement to a building: During term time, the children go to ____ every weekday to study.

explain.why: Anak-anak itu pergi buat belajar, sesuai fungsi sekolahnya. Makanya “go to school” tanpa artikel.
explain.rule: Nama lembaga nggak pakai artikel kalau maksudnya fungsinya: go to school, be in prison. Kalau maksudnya gedungnya, baru pakai “the”.
explain.memory: Belajar di sana sebagai murid pakai “go to school”.

distractors.misconception: focuses on a particular building instead of institutional attendance
distractors.whyFailsId: Soalnya jelas nanya fungsi sekolahnya, dan itu tanpa artikel: “go to school”.

distractors.misconception: introduces one unspecified building rather than the attendance idiom
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk ini nyebut satu tempat yang nggak tertentu.

distractors.misconception: turns one routine of attendance into a generic plural destination
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk jamak nyebut banyak tujuan yang umum.

items.sentence: I bumped into ____ at the airport yesterday.

explain.why: “A friend of mine” artinya salah satu temanku. Ini pola baku buat ngenalin satu dari beberapa teman.
explain.rule: Kepemilikan ganda: “a”, “an”, “this”, atau “that” + kata benda + “of” + kata ganti kepemilikan. Kata ganti kepemilikannya “mine”, “yours”, “his”, “hers”, “ours”, atau “theirs”.
explain.memory: “A friend of mine” berarti salah satu temanku.

distractors.misconception: Duplicates possession by using both 'my' and 'of mine' together.
distractors.whyFailsId: kepemilikannya kesebut dua kali dalam satu frasa.

distractors.misconception: Uses the object pronoun 'me' instead of the possessive pronoun 'mine' after 'of'.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata ganti objek dipakai di posisi kata ganti kepemilikan.

distractors.misconception: Uses definite article 'the' where the indefinite 'a' is required for introducing one of several friends.
distractors.whyFailsId: Pola kepemilikan ganda nggak pakai “the”. Polanya minta “a”, “an”, “this”, atau “that” di depan kata bendanya.

items.sentence: The fire alarm went off ____ the meeting, so everyone had to leave the building.

explain.why: “During the meeting” nyebut rentang waktu tempat alarmnya bunyi.
explain.rule: Pakai during + kata benda buat bilang sesuatu terjadi di dalam satu rentang waktu.
explain.memory: During + kata benda: during the meeting. While + subjek dan kata kerja: while we were meeting.

distractors.misconception: Applies duration preposition 'for' to a point-in-time event rather than a length of time.
distractors.whyFailsId: “for” ngukur lamanya, alarmnya cuma satu kejadian sekejap.

distractors.misconception: Confuses 'during' (within a period) with 'since' (marking a starting point).
distractors.whyFailsId: “since” nandain awal periode dan minta bentuk perfect.

distractors.misconception: Uses the conjunction 'while' where a preposition is grammatically required before a noun phrase.
distractors.whyFailsId: “while” minta subjek dan kata kerja di belakangnya.

items.sentence: To use the conventional collocation for directly evaluating a specific result: I'm really pleased ____ your exam results.

explain.why: Soalnya minta pasangan kata buat nilai satu hasil tertentu. “Pleased with” yang lazim buat itu.
explain.rule: “Pleased with” buat orang, penampilan, atau hasil tertentu. “Pleased about” buat sebuah keadaan. “Pleased for” + orang buat ikut seneng atas keberuntungannya.
explain.memory: Hasil pakai “with”, kabar pakai “about”, orang pakai “for”.

distractors.misconception: uses the broader situation-focused pattern instead of directly evaluating the result
distractors.whyFailsId: “pleased about” fokus ke keadaan yang lebih luas.

distractors.misconception: confuses pleased with pleased for someone
distractors.whyFailsId: “pleased for” berarti ikut seneng buat orang lain.

distractors.misconception: imports a preposition that does not collocate with pleased
distractors.whyFailsId: “pleased on” bukan pasangan kata yang baku.

items.sentence: ____ regularly is one of the best things you can do for your long-term health.

explain.why: “Exercising” sebagai subjek bentuk -ing itu cara yang wajar buat bikin pernyataan umum soal sebuah kegiatan.
explain.rule: Bentuk -ing biasanya jadi subjek kalimat buat pernyataan umum soal sebuah kegiatan.
explain.memory: Kegiatan sebagai subjek pakai bentuk -ing: Exercising, Reading, Smoking, terus kata kerjanya.

distractors.misconception: Blends the infinitive marker 'to' with a gerund ending, producing an invalid hybrid.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to” harus diikuti kata kerja bentuk dasar, bukan bentuk -ing.

distractors.misconception: Places 'to' after the verb instead of before it, misreading the infinitive structure.
distractors.whyFailsId: urutan ini nggak bikin susunan subjek yang sah dalam Bahasa Inggris.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'for' as if introducing purpose rather than a subject.
distractors.whyFailsId: “for exercise” kebaca sebagai frasa tujuan yang belum lengkap.

items.sentence: The book ___ I borrowed from the library was due back yesterday.

explain.why: Kata yang hilang jadi objek dari “borrowed”: the book that I borrowed. Bendanya buku, jadi pakai “that” atau “which”, bukan “what”.
explain.rule: Anak kalimat penjelas buat benda pakai “that” atau “which”. Kalau posisinya objek, katanya malah boleh dihilangin: “The book I borrowed” juga benar.
explain.memory: Benda pakai “that” atau “which”. “What” nggak pernah nempel ke kata benda kayak “the book”.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'what' as a relative pronoun, a common cross-linguistic transfer error.
distractors.whyFailsId: “what” nggak bisa nempel ke kata benda kayak “the book”.

distractors.misconception: Uses a personal relative pronoun for a non-human antecedent.
distractors.whyFailsId: “who” buat orang, padahal “the book” itu benda.

items.sentence: This new laptop is ____ faster than my old one.

explain.why: “Faster” itu bentuk perbandingan. Penguat bakunya “much”, bareng “far” dan “a lot”.
explain.rule: Kuatin bentuk perbandingan pakai “much”, “far”, “a lot”, atau “a bit”. Jangan pakai “very”, “so”, atau “too”.
explain.memory: Contohnya “much faster”, “far better”, dan “a lot cheaper”.

distractors.misconception: Transfers the common absolute-adjective intensifier 'very' onto a comparative form.
distractors.whyFailsId: “very faster” nggak sah dalam Bahasa Inggris.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'so', which needs a following 'that'-clause or exclamatory context, as a plain intensifier before a comparative.
distractors.whyFailsId: “so” biasanya langsung ketemu kata sifat aja, nggak bawa kata benda.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'too' (meaning excessive) as if it were a neutral intensifier.
distractors.whyFailsId: “too” nyiratin kelebihan yang nggak diinginkan.

items.sentence: A: "I saw a UFO last night." B: "You saw ____?"

explain.why: “You saw what?” ngulang urutan kata pernyataannya persis. Cuma bagian yang bikin heran yang diganti kata tanya.
explain.rule: Pertanyaan ulang nahan urutan kata pernyataan tanpa pembalikan. Kata tanyanya ditaruh tepat di tempat keterangan yang bikin heran.
explain.memory: Pertanyaan ulang ngulang, bukan ngebalik.

distractors.misconception: Forms a standard inverted question instead of echoing the statement's structure.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk ini balik ke pembalikan subjek dan kata bantu.

distractors.misconception: Fully reformulates the question with standard word order rather than echoing.
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimatnya disusun ulang penuh pakai urutan pertanyaan baku.

distractors.misconception: Uses a gerund fragment instead of the statement's original verb form.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk -ing bukan pola pertanyaan ulang yang dikenal.

items.sentence: ____ the heavy rain, the outdoor concert went ahead as planned.

explain.why: “Despite” itu preposition (kata depan) yang bisa langsung diikuti frasa benda kayak “the heavy rain”.
explain.rule: Despite dan in spite of diikuti kata benda atau bentuk -ing. Although, even though, dan though diikuti anak kalimat berisi subjek dan kata kerja.
explain.memory: Despite + kata benda; although + anak kalimat.

distractors.misconception: Assumes 'although' can be followed directly by a noun phrase like 'despite' can.
distractors.whyFailsId: “although” harus diikuti anak kalimat utuh, bukan frasa benda telanjang.

distractors.misconception: Treats 'however' as a subordinating connector that can start a sentence and directly attach to a noun.
distractors.whyFailsId: “however” itu kata keterangan kalimat yang butuh anak kalimat sendiri.

distractors.misconception: Confuses 'even though' (also clause-requiring, like 'although') with prepositional 'despite'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “even though” juga minta anak kalimat utuh, bukan frasa benda telanjang.

items.sentence: Original: Sarah broke the vase, not her brother. Cleft emphasis: ____ broke the vase, not her brother.

explain.why: “It was Sarah that broke the vase” ngikutin kerangka it-cleft yang baku. Urutannya: It, bentuk be, bagian yang ditonjolin, that, sisa anak kalimatnya.
explain.rule: It-cleft: It + was atau is + bagian yang ditonjolin + that + sisa kalimat aslinya.
explain.memory: It was [yang ditonjolin] that [sisanya] — jangan pernah misahin “It was”.

distractors.misconception: Misorders the fixed cleft frame, inserting the emphasized element before 'was'.
distractors.whyFailsId: kerangka cleft minta “It was” tetap nyatu persis sebelum bagian yang ditonjolin.

distractors.misconception: Fronts the emphasized noun before the cleft frame entirely.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata benda yang ditonjolin naik bahkan sebelum kata “it”, jadi kerangka wajibnya nggak kepakai.

distractors.misconception: Places 'that' before the emphasized noun instead of after it.
distractors.whyFailsId: “that” wajib berdiri sesudah bagian yang ditonjolin buat mbuka sisa anak kalimatnya.

items.sentence: When I was a child, I ____ a small village near the mountains.

explain.why: “Live” itu kata kerja keadaan. “Used to live” nyatain keadaan lampau yang sekarang udah nggak berlaku.
explain.rule: “Used to” nyakup keadaan lampau dan tindakan berulang. “Would” cuma nyakup tindakan berulang, nggak pernah keadaan.
explain.memory: Keadaan lampau cuma “used to”; tindakan berulang boleh dua-duanya.

distractors.misconception: Applies 'would' to a stative verb (live = residing state) as if it were a repeated dynamic action.
distractors.whyFailsId: “would” disediain buat tindakan berulang kayak “would visit”.

distractors.misconception: Adds a past-tense ending to the verb after the modal 'would'.
distractors.whyFailsId: modal selalu diikutin kata kerja bentuk dasar.

distractors.misconception: Uses a bare gerund with no finite verb to carry the sentence's tense.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk -ing sendirian nggak bisa jadi kata kerja utama.

items.sentence: So far this week I ___ three important emails, and there are two more to write before Friday.

explain.why: “So far this week” nyebut rentang yang belum tutup, dan dua surel lagi belum kekirim. Jadi present perfect yang pas di sini.
explain.rule: Pilih present perfect daripada past simple buat tindakan di dalam rentang yang belum berakhir. Bentuk lampau justru nutup rentang yang masih jalan.
explain.memory: Rentang waktunya belum tutup, berarti pakai present perfect.

distractors.misconception: Uses past simple because a specific number of emails is mentioned.
distractors.whyFailsId: “so far” nandain rentang yang masih jalan, jadi bentuk lampau nggak pas.

distractors.misconception: Uses past continuous to describe a series of completed actions.
distractors.whyFailsId: past continuous cocok buat tindakan yang lagi jalan di satu saat lampau.

distractors.misconception: Uses present simple, ignoring that the sentence reports completed past actions within the current period.
distractors.whyFailsId: present simple nggambarin kebiasaan atau fakta.

items.sentence: Which completion explicitly criticizes the past decision rather than merely noting a possibility? You ____ more carefully before signing the contract — now we're stuck with these terms.

explain.why: “Should have read” negur kelalaian baca yang teliti, dan itu sejalan sama akibat yang disesalin di kalimatnya.
explain.rule: Should have + bentuk ke-3 berarti teguran atau penyesalan atas tindakan lampau yang nggak dilakuin atau keliru dilakuin.
explain.memory: Ada penyesalan atas kelalaian di masa lalu? Pakai should have.

distractors.misconception: Treats a clearly critical statement as a neutral, non-judgmental missed opportunity.
distractors.whyFailsId: “now we’re stuck with these terms” nyatain penyesalan, bukan peluang netral.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'would have' as if this were a hypothetical conditional result rather than direct criticism.
distractors.whyFailsId: “would have” biasanya pasangan anak kalimat if buat hasil pengandaian.

distractors.misconception: Confuses past deduction ('must have') with retrospective criticism.
distractors.whyFailsId: “must have read” nyimpulin dia kemungkinan besar udah baca, bentrok sama maksud kalimatnya.

items.sentence: After months of treatment, she hopes to ___ walk without assistance again.

explain.why: “Hopes to” minta bentuk dasar sesudahnya. “Be able to” nyediain bentuk kemampuan yang nggak dimiliki “can”.
explain.rule: “Can” nggak punya bentuk “to” dan bentuk perfect. Kalau susunannya minta bentuk kayak itu, pakai “be able to”.
explain.memory: Nggak ada “to can”; ucapin “to be able to”.

distractors.misconception: places the finite modal 'can' after infinitive 'to'
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk “to can” nggak dikenal dalam Bahasa Inggris.

distractors.misconception: uses a finite past/conditional modal in a non-finite slot
distractors.whyFailsId: “could” modal bertense yang nggak bisa nyusul “hopes to”.

distractors.misconception: uses a gerund-participle where a bare infinitive is required
