distractors.whyFailsId: “to” yang pertama minta bentuk dasar bukan bentuk -ing.

items.sentence: In formal written English, which completion presents his fear as an ongoing trait he still has, rather than only a past state? If he ____ so afraid of flying, he would have joined us on the trip to Japan last year.

explain.why: “Weren’t” berbentuk second conditional dan nyatain sifat sekarang yang nggak nyata, yaitu rasa takutnya. Itu yang nerangin kenapa hasil lampaunya nggak kejadian.
explain.rule: Mixed conditional sebab masa kini dan hasil masa lalu: If + past simple atau bentuk were, terus would have + past participle.
explain.memory: Sebab masa kini dan hasil masa lalu: If + were ..., would have + past participle.

distractors.misconception: Forces the third conditional past perfect form into the condition clause, matching the past result tense.
distractors.whyFailsId: bahasanya bener, tapi rasa takutnya jadi keadaan lampau saja, nggak kebawa sampai sekarang.

distractors.misconception: Uses ordinary past simple negative instead of the subjunctive 'weren't' required in hypothetical conditionals.
distractors.whyFailsId: pengandaian formal biasanya pakai “were” di anak kalimat if, bukan “was”.

distractors.misconception: Uses present tense, missing that the condition is hypothetical/unreal, not a real current fact.
distractors.whyFailsId: present simple bakal nyatain fakta nyata, padahal syaratnya cuma dibayangin.

items.sentence: You can borrow my car ____ you bring it back before six o'clock.

explain.why: “Provided that” nyatain syarat positif yang harus dipenuhi biar izin minjem mobilnya tetap berlaku.
explain.rule: Provided that dan as long as nandain syarat positif yang wajib dipenuhi. Unless artinya “kecuali kalau”.
explain.memory: “Provided that” berarti cuma kalau; “unless” berarti kecuali kalau.

distractors.misconception: Uses the negative-exception connector where a positive required condition is meant.
distractors.whyFailsId: “unless” berarti kecuali kalau, jadi maknanya kebalik dari syarat yang dimaksud.

distractors.misconception: Uses a concessive connector implying the condition doesn't matter to the outcome.
distractors.whyFailsId: “even if” bilang hasilnya tetap kejadian apa pun syaratnya.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'in case' (precaution for a possible future event) instead of a condition of permission.
distractors.whyFailsId: “in case” nyatain persiapan buat sesuatu yang mungkin kejadian.

items.sentence: The company sent all employees a bonus. → All employees ____ a bonus.

explain.why: “Were sent a bonus” bikin penerimanya, yaitu para karyawan, jadi subjek pasifnya. Objek langsungnya tetap berdiri sesudah kata kerjanya.
explain.rule: Di kata kerja berobjek dua, objek penerimanya biasanya jadi subjek pasif, terus disusul objek langsungnya.
explain.memory: Penerimanya jadi subjek: “Employees were sent a bonus”, tanpa “to”.

distractors.misconception: Adds an unnecessary preposition after the passive verb when the recipient is already the subject.
distractors.whyFailsId: begitu “all employees” jadi subjek, “to” jadi mubazir.

distractors.misconception: Reverses the auxiliary and main verb order.
distractors.whyFailsId: “sent were” bukan urutan kata yang sah buat kalimat pasif.

distractors.misconception: Fails subject-verb agreement, treating the plural subject 'all employees' as singular.
distractors.whyFailsId: “all employees” bentuknya jamak, jadi kata bantunya nggak boleh tunggal.

items.sentence: She resents ____ like a child in front of her colleagues.

explain.why: “Being treated” itu bentuk -ing pasif yang pas jadi pelengkap “resent”, kata kerja yang minta objek bentuk -ing.
explain.rule: Bentuk -ing pasif being + past participle nyusul kata kerja atau kata depan yang minta pelengkap -ing. Contohnya resent, avoid, dan admit.
explain.memory: Resent, avoid, dan admit diikuti being + past participle, nggak pernah “to be”.

distractors.misconception: Applies the passive infinitive pattern to a verb ('resent') that specifically requires a gerund complement.
distractors.whyFailsId: “resent” diikuti bentuk -ing, bukan bentuk to, jadi pola pasifnya ikut salah.

distractors.misconception: Uses the bare passive infinitive without 'to' or the required gerund '-ing' form.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk ini cocok sesudah modal atau sesudah make dan let, bukan sesudah “resent”.

distractors.misconception: Drops the auxiliary needed to mark the passive voice, leaving only the past participle.
distractors.whyFailsId: tanda pasifnya hilang sama sekali, jadi kalimatnya nggak utuh sesudah “resents”.

items.sentence: He apologized ____ late to the meeting.

explain.why: “Apologized for being late” pakai pola tetap apologize + for + bentuk -ing buat nyebut alasan minta maafnya.
explain.rule: Apologize for + bentuk -ing buat nyebut alasannya; deny + bentuk -ing sebagai objek langsung. Dua-duanya beda dari pola kata kerja + anak kalimat that.
explain.memory: “Apologize” FOR + bentuk -ing buat alasannya; “deny” + bentuk -ing tanpa kata depan.

distractors.misconception: Applies the generic reporting pattern (verb + that-clause) to a verb requiring preposition + gerund.
distractors.whyFailsId: “apologize” biasanya nggak langsung diikuti anak kalimat “that” di susunan ini.

distractors.misconception: Uses an infinitive complement instead of the required preposition + gerund pattern.
distractors.whyFailsId: “apologize to be late” bukan pola yang baku dalam Bahasa Inggris.

distractors.misconception: Uses the bare base form after the preposition 'for' instead of the required gerund.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata depan harus diikuti bentuk -ing, bukan kata kerja dasar.

items.sentence: My cousin has lived in ____ Netherlands for almost ten years now.

explain.why: Nama negaranya berbentuk jamak: “Netherlands”. Nama negara kayak gitu selalu pakai “the”.
explain.rule: Kebanyakan nama negara nggak pakai artikel. Tapi nama jamak kayak the Netherlands dan the Philippines pakai “the”. Nama dengan United atau Republic juga pakai “the”.
explain.memory: Nama negara yang kedengeran jamak pakai “the”: “the Netherlands”, “the Philippines”, “the United States”.

distractors.misconception: Treats the country name as an ordinary countable noun needing an indefinite article.
distractors.whyFailsId: Nama negara nggak pakai “a”. “The Netherlands” itu pengecualian tetap yang wajib pakai “the”.

distractors.misconception: Applies the indefinite article rule based on the following vowel sound, ignoring that country names don't take indefinite articles at all.
distractors.whyFailsId: Nama negara nggak pakai “an”. Nama tetap ini wajib pakai “the”: the Netherlands.

distractors.misconception: Overgeneralizes the common 'no article before country names' rule to every country name.
distractors.whyFailsId: nama negara ini masuk pengecualian, jadi celahnya nggak boleh kosong.

items.sentence: I have exactly two close friends. ____ them live in different countries now, so we rarely meet in person.

explain.why: “Them” itu kata ganti objek. Jadi kata jumlahnya butuh “of” di depannya.
explain.rule: Pakai kata jumlah + “of” sebelum kata ganti objek. Contohnya “both of them”, “all of us”, dan “neither of you”.
explain.memory: Ada kata ganti objek di depan? Pakai “of”.

distractors.misconception: drops 'of' before the object pronoun
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk ini ngilangin “of” yang diwajibin di depan “them”.

distractors.misconception: drops 'of' and ignores the explicitly two-person set
distractors.whyFailsId: “all them” nggak sah dalam Bahasa Inggris baku.

distractors.misconception: drops 'of' and reverses the affirmative meaning
distractors.whyFailsId: “neither” juga ngebalik makna kalimatnya jadi negatif.

items.sentence: We regret ___ you that your application has been unsuccessful.

explain.why: Kalimat ini baru nyampein kabar penolakannya sekarang, jadi “regret” minta bentuk to: “to inform”.
explain.rule: Regret + bentuk to berarti nyampein kabar buruk secara resmi. Regret + bentuk -ing berarti nyesalin tindakan yang udah lewat. “Mean” dan “go on” ikut keluarga pola yang sama, tapi kartu di lesson ini cuma nguji “regret”.
explain.memory: Regret TO INFORM you sekarang; regret DOING sesuatu di masa lalu.

distractors.misconception: Uses the gerund pattern (regretting a past action) where the formal-announcement meaning is intended.
distractors.whyFailsId: “regret informing” berarti nyesal karena udah terlanjur ngasih tahu, padahal kabarnya baru disampein sekarang.

distractors.misconception: Uses a perfect gerund implying the informing already happened before the regret.
distractors.whyFailsId: “having informed” naruh kabarnya seolah udah selesai disampein sebelum penyesalannya muncul.

distractors.misconception: Drops the infinitive marker 'to' entirely.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar tanpa “to” bukan pelengkap yang pas buat “regret” di makna resmi ini.

items.sentence: Which completion most explicitly marks the breaking as earlier than the later admission? He admitted ____ the vase.

explain.why: “Having broken” negesin bahwa pecahnya vas terjadi sebelum pengakuannya.
explain.rule: Bentuk -ing perfect having + past participle negesin tindakannya mendahului kata kerja utama. Bentuk -ing sederhana ninggalin urutannya tersirat.
explain.memory: Having + past participle berarti tegas lebih dulu.

distractors.misconception: Uses the simple gerund, which leaves the earlier timing to context instead of encoding it explicitly.
distractors.whyFailsId: “breaking” memang sah buat “admit”, tapi urutan waktunya nggak ditegesin.

distractors.misconception: Uses an infinitive complement after 'admit', a verb that takes a gerund, not an infinitive.
distractors.whyFailsId: “admit” nggak diikuti bentuk to di Bahasa Inggris baku, kata ini minta pelengkap -ing.

distractors.misconception: Uses the bare base form with no verb marking at all.
distractors.whyFailsId: “admit break” nggak punya fungsi tata bahasa yang sah, dan kata kerja dasar nggak pernah diterima.

items.sentence: The charity has over two hundred volunteers, ____ are retired teachers.

explain.why: “Many of whom” madukan kata jumlah sama kata penghubung “whom” buat nunjuk balik ke “volunteers”.
explain.rule: Kata jumlah + of + whom atau which nyambungin anak kalimat penjelas ke sebagian kelompok yang udah disebut. Contohnya many of whom dan some of which.
explain.memory: Many of whom dan some of which — kata jumlah dulu, terus “of”, terus kata penghubungnya.

distractors.misconception: Reverses the order of quantifier and relative pronoun.
distractors.whyFailsId: “which many” naruh kata penghubung sebelum kata jumlah, dan “which” juga nggak bisa buat orang.

distractors.misconception: Scrambles the word order of the fixed quantifier + of + whom structure.
distractors.whyFailsId: urutan ini bukan pola yang dikenal, rangkaiannya wajib kata jumlah dulu, baru “of”.

distractors.misconception: Uses a personal pronoun 'them' instead of a relative pronoun, which cannot join two clauses.
distractors.whyFailsId: “them” bukan kata penghubung, jadi dua anak kalimatnya cuma nyambung koma.

items.sentence: ____ the window during the storm last night?

explain.why: “Who” di sini pelaku yang mecahin jendelanya. Jadi urutannya tetap kayak pernyataan, tanpa kata bantu.
explain.rule: Pertanyaan tentang subjek pakai urutan kata pernyataan, tanpa kata bantu do, does, atau did.
explain.memory: Pertanyaan tentang subjek: Who + kata kerja, tanpa do atau did.

distractors.misconception: Adds the auxiliary 'did' as if this were an object question, following the standard question-formation rule mechanically.
distractors.whyFailsId: “did” disisipin kayak ini pertanyaan tentang objek.

distractors.misconception: Adds 'did' and keeps the past-tense main verb form together.
distractors.whyFailsId: “did” dan “broke” bawa bentuk lampau dua kali.

distractors.misconception: Uses present-tense auxiliary 'does' for a clearly past-time event ('last night').
distractors.whyFailsId: “does” itu bentuk present, bentrok sama “last night”.

items.sentence: She whispered the instructions ____ the other students wouldn't hear.

explain.why: Anak kalimat tujuannya punya subjek sendiri, yaitu “the other students”. “So that” yang bisa nampung itu.
explain.rule: “So that” diikutin anak kalimat utuh dan subjeknya boleh beda. “In order to” dan “so as to” diikutin kata kerja dasar dengan subjek yang sama.
explain.memory: Subjek beda pakai “so that”; subjek sama pakai “in order to”.

distractors.misconception: Uses the infinitive-purpose connector before a full clause with a different subject.
distractors.whyFailsId: “in order to” minta subjek yang sama kayak induk kalimatnya.

distractors.misconception: Uses another infinitive-purpose connector requiring the same subject, mismatching the different-subject clause.
distractors.whyFailsId: “so as to” minta kata kerja dasar tanpa subjek baru.

distractors.misconception: Uses a preposition that cannot introduce a full purpose clause.
distractors.whyFailsId: “for” cuma bisa diikutin frasa benda.

items.sentence: Which formal conjunctive adverb best completes this academic passage? The study's sample size was too small to generalize the findings. ____, the participants were not randomly selected, further weakening the results.

explain.why: “Furthermore” itu conjunctive adverb resmi buat nambah satu butir pendukung di tulisan akademik.
explain.rule: Conjunctive adverb penambahan yang resmi antara lain furthermore dan moreover. Padanan percakapannya antara lain plus dan what is more.
explain.memory: Penambahan buat ragam akademik: furthermore atau moreover.

distractors.misconception: Selects a conversational addition phrase instead of a formal conjunctive adverb.
distractors.whyFailsId: “what’s more” memang nambah keterangan, tapi nadanya percakapan dan soalnya minta ragam akademik.

distractors.misconception: Uses a casual spoken connector in a formal academic passage.
distractors.whyFailsId: “plus” bernada santai, bukan conjunctive adverb resmi yang diminta soalnya.

distractors.misconception: Uses a coordinating conjunction instead of the requested conjunctive adverb.
distractors.whyFailsId: “and” itu conjunction, bukan conjunctive adverb yang secara tegas diminta soalnya.

items.sentence: ____ such a disorganized meeting before — nothing was decided at all.

explain.why: “Never have I attended” majuin “Never” terus mbalik kata bantu “have” ke depan subjek “I”. Itu pola penekanan yang diwajibin.
explain.rule: Majuin keterangan negatif atau pembatas kayak never, rarely, not only, dan seldom demi penekanan mewajibin pembalikan subjek dan kata bantunya.
explain.memory: Never + kata bantu + subjek: “Never have I ...”, “Rarely does she ...”.

distractors.misconception: Fronts the negative adverbial without applying the required subject-auxiliary inversion.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata bantu “have” udah ada tapi tetap di belakang subjek, padahal “Never” di depan mewajibinnya maju.

distractors.misconception: Fronts 'Never' with no auxiliary at all, ignoring both the inversion rule and the need for 'have' with 'before'.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata bantunya nggak ada sama sekali, padahal makna “never before” minta bentuk present perfect.

distractors.misconception: Places 'never' after the auxiliary instead of at the very front of the sentence.
distractors.whyFailsId: di pola penekanan ini “Never” wajib jadi kata pertama, bukan kata bantunya.

items.sentence: ____ of the earthquake that entire buildings collapsed within seconds.

explain.why: “Such was the impact” majuin “such” dengan pembalikan penuh antara kata kerja dan subjeknya. Itu pola penekanan sastra yang udah tetap.
explain.rule: Such + was atau were + subjek + that + anak kalimat akibat itu pola pembalikan tetap di ragam resmi atau sastra.
explain.memory: Such was the impact that ... — “such” memimpin, kata kerjanya langsung nyusul.

distractors.misconception: Fronts 'such' but fails to invert the verb 'was' before the subject.
distractors.whyFailsId: pola ini minta pembalikan penuh kata kerja dan subjek sesudah “such” dimajuin.

distractors.misconception: Keeps normal subject-first order and misplaces 'such' mid-sentence.
distractors.whyFailsId: Subjeknya masih di depan dan “such” cuma nyelip di tengah. Jadi nggak ada pembalikan sama sekali.

distractors.misconception: Treats the sentence as a yes/no question by fronting only the verb.
distractors.whyFailsId: susunan ini keluar sebagai urutan pertanyaan, padahal kalimatnya pernyataan dramatis.

items.sentence: These days my brother ___ coffee every morning.

explain.why: “My brother” sama kayak he. Kebiasaan tiap pagi, jadi kata kerjanya “drinks”.
explain.rule: Present simple positif buat he, she, dan it. Kata kerjanya dapat akhiran -s atau -es.
explain.memory: He, she, it: kata kerjanya dapat -s.

distractors.misconception: base-form overuse
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar, padahal subjeknya orang ketiga tunggal.

distractors.misconception: progressive confusion
distractors.whyFailsId: nggak ada kata bantu, dan kalimatnya soal kebiasaan.

distractors.misconception: past-tense confusion
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk lampau, padahal “these days” nunjuk sekarang.

items.sentence: They ___ at home today.

explain.why: “They” itu jamak. Bentuk be buat jamak ya “are”.
explain.rule: Bentuk be sekarang: I am. He, she, it is. You, we, they are.
explain.memory: “They” selalu sama “are”: “they are at home”.

distractors.misconception: first-person be
distractors.whyFailsId: dipakai bareng I, bukan bareng they.

distractors.misconception: singular be
distractors.whyFailsId: buat satu orang, padahal “they” itu jamak.

distractors.misconception: base form
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar, nggak bisa jadi kata kerja utama.

items.sentence: There ___ two books on the table.

explain.why: Bendanya “two books”, jumlahnya lebih dari satu. Jadi pakai “are”.
explain.rule: There are plus kata benda jamak. There is plus kata benda tunggal.
explain.memory: Banyak: “there are”. Satu: “there is”.

distractors.misconception: singular agreement
distractors.whyFailsId: buat satu benda, padahal “two books” lebih dari satu.

distractors.misconception: base form
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar, nggak bisa jadi kata kerja utama.

distractors.misconception: past tense
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk lampau, padahal kalimatnya soal keadaan sekarang.

items.sentence: Anna is my friend. ___ brother is a doctor.

explain.why: Sesudah bagian kosong ada kata benda “brother”. “Her” bikin jelas brother-nya punya Anna.
explain.rule: Sebelum kata benda pakai kata kepemilikan. Contohnya my, your, his, her, its, our, their.
explain.memory: Her plus kata benda; hers jalan sendiri.

distractors.misconception: subject pronoun
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk subjek, nggak bisa langsung nerangin “brother”.

distractors.misconception: possessive pronoun
distractors.whyFailsId: berdiri sendiri, nggak pernah diikuti kata benda.

distractors.misconception: object pronoun
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk objek, bukan kata kepemilikan.

items.sentence: My sister ___ swim, but she cannot drive.

explain.why: Kalimat ini soal bisa atau nggak bisa. “Can swim” artinya mampu berenang.
explain.rule: Can plus kata kerja dasar buat nyatain kemampuan. Tanpa to, tanpa -s.
explain.memory: Can plus kata kerja dasar: can swim, can drive.

distractors.misconception: be verb
distractors.whyFailsId: nggak nyatain kemampuan bareng bentuk dasar “swim”.

distractors.misconception: do auxiliary
distractors.whyFailsId: nggak bikin kalimat kemampuan di sini.

distractors.misconception: possession
distractors.whyFailsId: artinya punya atau ngalamin, bukan mampu.

items.sentence: Which completion presents the start as something that would still be under way on that future day? If the board had approved the budget last month, construction ___ next Monday.

explain.why: Persetujuan yang nggak nyata itu ada di bulan lalu. Pembangunan yang dibayangin ada di Senin depan. “Would be starting” jagain hubungan lintas waktu itu.
explain.rule: Mixed conditional bisa madukan if + past perfect buat sebab lampau yang nggak nyata. Akibat masa kini atau masa depannya pakai would + kata kerja dasar atau bentuk berkelanjutan.
explain.memory: Sebab lampau dan akibat masa depan: if had done, would be doing.

distractors.misconception: moves the result into the unreal past
distractors.whyFailsId: “would have” di sini sah, tapi dimulainya jadi satu kejadian tuntas, bukan yang sedang jalan.

distractors.misconception: treats the future result as real despite the unreal past condition
distractors.whyFailsId: anggarannya nggak disetujui, jadi mulainya cuma dibayangin dan minta “would”.

distractors.misconception: uses simple past for an explicitly future consequence
distractors.whyFailsId: past simple bentrok sama “next Monday” dan nggak nandain akibatnya cuma dibayangin.

items.sentence: At 9 p.m. the office lights were on and keyboards could be heard, so the team ___ late at that moment.

explain.why: “Must have been working” madukan kesimpulan kuat, acuan waktu lampau, dan kegiatan yang sedang jalan jam sembilan malam.
explain.rule: Buat kesimpulan kuat soal kegiatan yang sedang jalan di satu saat lampau, pakai must have been + kata kerja -ing.
explain.memory: Bukti kuat plus kegiatan lampau yang sedang jalan: must have been working.

distractors.misconception: uses a completed-event deduction instead of an ongoing past activity
distractors.whyFailsId: “at that moment” dan suara kegiatannya mbingkai pekerjaannya sedang jalan, jadi butuh bentuk berkelanjutan.

distractors.misconception: changes evidence-based deduction into present advice or expectation
distractors.whyFailsId: “should work” nggak nunjuk saat lampau yang diamati dan nggak nyatain kesimpulan dari bukti.

distractors.misconception: reverses the polarity of the evidence
distractors.whyFailsId: lampu nyala dan suara papan ketik justru ndukung kesimpulan bahwa timnya kerja.

items.sentence: Only after the second audit ___ the scale of the error.

explain.why: “Only after” di depan maksa “did” naik ke depan “the board”, dan “understand” tetap bentuk dasar.
explain.rule: Waktu frasa pembatas yang dibuka “only” dimajuin, balik kata bantu dan subjek di induk kalimatnya. Polanya: Only after X did + subjek + kata kerja dasar.
explain.memory: Only after ... did + subjek + kata kerja dasar.

distractors.misconception: keeps ordinary statement order after a fronted restrictive phrase
distractors.whyFailsId: urutan pernyataan biasa dipertahanin tanpa kata bantu, jadi isyarat “Only after” di depan nggak ditindaklanjuti.

distractors.misconception: inverts the lexical verb directly
distractors.whyFailsId: “understood the board” mbalik kata kerja utamanya, bukan kata bantunya, jadi susunannya rusak.

distractors.misconception: adds emphatic do but does not invert it with the subject
distractors.whyFailsId: kata bantunya ada tapi tetap berdiri sesudah subjek, jadi pembalikannya belum terjadi.

items.sentence: What the team needed most ___ a clear decision.

explain.why: Seluruh anak kalimat what jadi satu subjek tunggal, dan “was” nyambungin langsung ke “a clear decision”.
explain.rule: Pola penekanan pakai what: What + anak kalimat + be + bagian yang ditonjolin. Anak kalimat what itu satu kesatuan subjek.
explain.memory: What we needed was X — satu anak kalimat what, satu gagasan tunggal.

distractors.misconception: makes the verb agree with the nearby plural noun team
distractors.whyFailsId: Pilihan “were” menyesuaikan kata kerjanya dengan “team”, padahal subjeknya seluruh anak kalimat “What the team needed most”.

distractors.misconception: inserts an it-cleft linker into a pseudo-cleft
distractors.whyFailsId: pola ini nyambungin anak kalimat what langsung ke bagian yang ditonjolin, tanpa nambah “that”.

distractors.misconception: adds a dummy cleft subject and creates two competing subjects
distractors.whyFailsId: anak kalimat what udah jadi subjek, jadi nambah “it” bikin susunannya nggak sah.

items.sentence: ___ the evidence twice, the committee reopened the investigation.

explain.why: “Having reviewed” naruh peninjauannya sebelum “the committee reopened”, jadi urutan waktunya jelas.
explain.rule: Anak kalimat participle bentuk perfect: having + past participle nandain tindakan yang lebih dulu dan udah selesai.
explain.memory: Tindakan aktif yang lebih dulu: “having reviewed”. Tindakan pasif yang lebih dulu: “having been reviewed”.

distractors.misconception: past participle alone
distractors.whyFailsId: “reviewed” nggak nandain dengan jelas tindakan aktif yang lebih dulu di sini.

distractors.misconception: bare verb
distractors.whyFailsId: “having” digandeng kata kerja bentuk dasar, jadi rangkaian participle perfect-nya nggak pernah kebentuk.

distractors.misconception: gerund mismatch
distractors.whyFailsId: “to reviewing” bukan bentuk anak kalimat participle yang dibutuhin di sini.

items.sentence: Much as the proposal ___ to several members at last month's meeting, the board rejected it on practical grounds.

explain.why: Frasa “at last month's meeting” maku ceritanya di masa lampau, jadi “appealed” yang pas sesudah much as.
explain.rule: Much as + subjek + kata kerja artinya walaupun, meskipun kenyataannya begitu.
explain.memory: Much as + subjek + kata kerja bertense berarti walaupun.

distractors.misconception: present mismatch
distractors.whyFailsId: frasa “at last month's meeting” maku penilaiannya di masa lampau, jadi bentuk present bentrok.

distractors.misconception: participle fragment
distractors.whyFailsId: “appealing” nggak ngasih anak kalimat bertense yang diwajibin sesudah much as.

distractors.misconception: present-tense clash plus unnatural collocation
distractors.whyFailsId: “has appeal” memang klausa utuh, tapi present-nya bentrok bingkai lampau dan pasangan katanya nggak wajar.

items.sentence: She ___ got a new phone.

explain.why: “She” sekelompok sama he dan it. Kelompok itu pakai “has got”.
explain.rule: Pakai “have got” buat “I”, “you”, “we”, dan “they”. Pakai “has got” buat “he”, “she”, dan “it”.
explain.memory: “He”, “she”, “it”: has got. “I”, “you”, “we”, “they”: have got.

distractors.misconception: plural-form transfer
distractors.whyFailsId: buat I, you, we, dan they, bukan “she”.

distractors.misconception: be-verb substitution
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk be, jadi is got nggak nyatain punya.

distractors.misconception: double-auxiliary construction
distractors.whyFailsId: does got nggak pernah bener di bahasa Inggris.

items.sentence: They ___ football yesterday.

explain.why: “Yesterday” bilang kejadiannya udah selesai. Kata kerjanya jadi “played”.
explain.rule: Bentuk lampau beraturan biasanya nambah -ed. Sesudah did atau did not, kata kerjanya bentuk dasar.
explain.memory: Yesterday: play jadi played. Ingat did plus play.

distractors.misconception: missing-past-marking
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar sekarang, padahal “yesterday” nunjuk masa lalu.

distractors.misconception: third-person-present form
distractors.whyFailsId: buat he, she, atau it di masa sekarang.

distractors.misconception: progressive-form substitution
distractors.whyFailsId: butuh kata bantu kayak “were”, nggak bisa sendiri.

items.sentence: They ___ at school yesterday.

explain.why: “They” itu jamak. Bentuk lampaunya “were”.
explain.rule: Pakai “was” buat “I”, “he”, “she”, dan “it”. Pakai “were” buat “you”, “we”, dan “they”.
explain.memory: “They” pakai “were”. “She” pakai “was”.

distractors.misconception: singular-past transfer
distractors.whyFailsId: buat subjek tunggal, padahal “they” itu jamak.

distractors.misconception: present-tense substitution
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk sekarang, padahal “yesterday” nunjuk masa lalu.

distractors.misconception: bare-infinitive substitution
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar, nggak bisa jadi kata kerja utama.

items.sentence: She ___ dinner right now.

explain.why: “Right now” nunjuk saat ini juga. Jadi bentuknya “is cooking”.
explain.rule: Present continuous: am, is, atau are plus kata kerja -ing. Dipakai buat kejadian yang lagi berlangsung.
explain.memory: Lagi berlangsung: be plus -ing, kayak she is cooking.

distractors.misconception: bare-verb-without-auxiliary
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar sendirian, kurang kata bantunya.

distractors.misconception: present-simple-habit
distractors.whyFailsId: nyatain kebiasaan, padahal “right now” nunjuk saat ini.

distractors.misconception: missing-be-auxiliary
distractors.whyFailsId: kurang kata bantu di depannya.

items.sentence: ___ do you live?

explain.why: Jawaban buat kalimat ini nama tempat. Jadi kata tanyanya “Where”.
explain.rule: Who buat orang. What buat benda. Where buat tempat. When buat waktu. Why buat alasan.
explain.memory: Where buat tempat, when buat waktu, who buat orang.

distractors.misconception: thing-question substitution
distractors.whyFailsId: nanya benda atau kegiatan, bukan tempat tinggal.

distractors.misconception: time-question substitution
distractors.whyFailsId: nanya waktu, bukan lokasi tinggalnya.

distractors.misconception: reason-question substitution
distractors.whyFailsId: nanya alasan, bukan lokasi tinggalnya.

items.sentence: I don't have ___ money.

explain.why: Ada “don’t”, jadi kalimatnya negatif. “Money” juga nggak bisa dihitung satu-satu. Pasangan buat dua-duanya “any”.
explain.rule: Some biasanya buat kalimat positif. Any buat kalimat negatif dan kalimat tanya. Many buat benda yang bisa dihitung, much buat yang nggak bisa.
explain.memory: Negatif plus nggak bisa dihitung: I do not have any money.

distractors.misconception: positive-quantifier-in-negative
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang jumlahnya ada, padahal kalimatnya nyangkal.

distractors.misconception: singular-article-with-uncountable
distractors.whyFailsId: cuma buat benda satuan, dan “money” bukan begitu.

distractors.misconception: countable-quantity-substitution
distractors.whyFailsId: buat benda banyak yang bisa dihitung satu-satu.

items.sentence: ___ name is Sari.

explain.why: Sesudah bagian kosong ada kata benda “name”. Jadi pakai “Her”.
explain.rule: Kata ganti subjek jadi subjek. Kata ganti objek berdiri sesudah kata kerja. Kata kepemilikan kayak her berdiri sebelum kata benda. Hers berdiri sendiri.
explain.memory: “Her name”, tapi “the name is hers”.

distractors.misconception: subject-pronoun-before-noun
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk subjek, nggak bisa berdiri sebelum kata benda.

distractors.misconception: stand-alone-possessive-before-noun
distractors.whyFailsId: berdiri sendiri, nggak bisa nerangin kata benda sesudahnya.

distractors.misconception: object-pronoun-substitution
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk objek, nggak nyatain kepemilikan.
